stories.summary: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions received a $447 million contract from the U.S. Space Force for a missile tracking ground system. The award follows an earlier Space Force contract with Parsons for the Resilient Missile Warning Tracking medium Earth orbit satellite program's ground operations center.

stories.title: Tension rises between Israel and Lebanon as IDF occupies south of Litani river
stories.summary: Israel announced on March 24 that its military would seize control of southern Lebanon up to the Litani River. The ongoing campaign has killed at least 1,039 people and displaced over a million during more than three weeks of fighting with Hezbollah. The Iran-backed group has vowed to resist.

stories.title: Iran strikes put in question US-Israeli attacks's impact on military capabilities
stories.summary: Iranian drone strikes hit Tel Aviv, damaging residential buildings and injuring several people. The attacks raised questions about whether prior U.S.-Israeli strikes had significantly degraded Iran's military capabilities. Analysts noted Iran has launched sporadic strikes apparently aimed at preserving its arsenal.

stories.title: Kenya fuel retailers running short of supplies amid Middle East war
stories.summary: Hundreds of fuel retailers across Kenya are experiencing supply shortages linked to the ongoing war in the Middle East. The head of the Petroleum Outlets Association of Kenya attributed the disruptions to conflict-related impacts on global fuel supply chains.

stories.title: Israeli defences questioned as Iran continues to cause damage
stories.summary: Iranian missile strikes have caused damage inside Israel, prompting questions about the effectiveness of Israeli air defense systems in intercepting incoming ballistic missiles.

stories.title: Hezbollah calls on Lebanon to 'immediately reverse' expulsion of Iranian ambassador
stories.summary: Hezbollah demanded that Lebanon immediately reverse its decision to expel Iran's ambassador, calling the move a "sin." Lebanon's foreign ministry had withdrawn the accreditation of the Iranian ambassador on Tuesday and given him until Sunday to leave the country.

stories.title: UK’s King Charles will be patron for major Jewish security organization
stories.summary: King Charles III will serve as patron of the Community Security Trust, a major organization advising Britain's estimated 280,000 Jews on security matters. The announcement came one day after an arson attack in London targeted ambulances belonging to a Jewish group.

stories.title: Gaza Boxing Women: Punching through war, trauma and displacement
stories.summary: In Gaza, girls and young women have been rebuilding a boxing community amid ongoing conflict and displacement. Participants use the sport to cope with grief and trauma while challenging social norms.

stories.title: Israel announces territorial seizure in Lebanon up to Litani River
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Katz announced that Israeli forces would control remaining bridges and a security zone up to the Litani River in southern Lebanon. The directive was issued during a meeting with the military chief of staff.

stories.title: Man convicted of hate crime for attacking Israeli in New York after Oct. 7
stories.summary: Yehia Amin was convicted of a hate crime in New York for punching an Israeli tourist following the October 7 attacks and sentenced to 90 days in prison. Separately, a vandal who defaced the home of the Brooklyn Museum's Jewish director had a felony charge dropped.

stories.title: DIU soldiers destroy Russian Zircon missile launcher in Crimea
stories.summary: Specialists from the Unmanned Systems Department of Ukraine's Defense Intelligence (DIU) destroyed a Russian Zircon hypersonic missile launcher in occupied Crimea using drone operations.

stories.title: CERT warns ‘hostile actors’ could exploit supply chains to target national infrastructure
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Computer Emergency Response Team issued a cybersecurity advisory warning that hostile actors may exploit supply chain vulnerabilities to target critical national infrastructure, including power grids, banking systems, and defense networks. The advisory noted that even minor lapses in hardware and software delivery could trigger large-scale failures.

stories.title: Iran parliament speaker: ‘No negotiations with the US’
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf stated on Monday that Iran is not engaged in negotiations with the United States to end the ongoing war.

stories.title: Aid flotilla reaches Cuba amid US oil blockade and blackouts
stories.summary: An aid flotilla has reached Cuba as a US-imposed oil blockade causes severe fuel shortages and widespread power blackouts across the island nation.

stories.title: Israeli hitmakers launch unexpected global chart topper
stories.summary: Israeli music group Temper City released their debut single 'Self Aware,' which reached number one on both TikTok and Spotify's global viral charts.

stories.title: At Least 1 Killed in Apartment Explosion in Annexed Crimea
stories.summary: At least one person was killed in an explosion at an apartment building in Russian-annexed Crimea. Investigators are working to determine the cause but have ruled out a gas leak.

stories.title: Top official says US still assessing how to test nuclear weapons
stories.summary: US Undersecretary of State Thomas DiNanno told a Senate committee that the administration is still assessing how to carry out President Donald Trump's order to resume nuclear weapons testing. He said no discussions have taken place regarding atmospheric nuclear tests.

stories.title: Woman shot dead in Galilee, taking 2026 toll in Arab community to 74
stories.summary: A woman, approximately 35 years old, was shot and killed in an agricultural area in the town of Reineh in the Galilee region. Her death brings the 2026 homicide toll in Israel's Arab community to 74 and marks the fifth female homicide victim this year amid ongoing organized crime violence.

stories.title: Who wins what in the EU's new trade deal with Australia?
stories.summary: The European Union and Australia have finalized a long-delayed free trade agreement. The deal comes as both parties face pressure from US tariffs and Chinese industrial competition, prompting them to resolve previous trade disputes.

stories.title: 'I intend to go back to my country': Exiled Ugandan opposition leader Bobi Wine
stories.summary: Exiled Ugandan opposition leader Bobi Wine told FRANCE 24 that he intends to return to Uganda after resurfacing in Washington following nearly two months in hiding. Wine said he remains under threat and called for international sanctions against President Yoweri Museveni and his son.

stories.title: Why is Pakistan being touted as mediator between US and Iran?
stories.summary: Pakistan is positioning itself as a potential mediator between the United States and Iran should either side agree to engage in talks aimed at resolving their conflict.

stories.title: Iranian missile intercepted over Lebanese airspace: Report
stories.summary: An Iranian missile was intercepted over Lebanese airspace for the first time on Tuesday, according to three senior Lebanese security sources. Two sources said a foreign naval vessel carried out the interception. Shrapnel reportedly fell over towns north of Beirut, causing light injuries.

stories.title: Israel prepares to mobilise 400,000 reservists in Lebanon war
stories.summary: Israel is preparing to mobilize up to 400,000 military reservists as it escalates operations against Lebanon. Deadly airstrikes have intensified even as ground advances remain limited.

stories.title: Bradley replacement is still on track, says Army acquisitions boss
stories.summary: The US Army's acquisitions chief confirmed that the program to replace the Bradley infantry fighting vehicle remains on schedule. The update came one year into the Army Transformation Initiative, which also includes a drone marketplace and other modernization efforts.

stories.title: North Korea’s Kim vows ‘irreversible’ nuclear status, warns Seoul of ‘merciless’ response
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un declared that the country's nuclear-armed status is irreversible and will never be relinquished. In a policy address to the Supreme People's Assembly, Kim said South Korea would soon be designated the "most hostile state" and accused the United States of committing "state terrorism."

stories.title: Terrorist attack in Bucha: Court orders suspect held without bail
stories.summary: A Kyiv district court ordered the suspect in the Bucha terrorist bombing to be held in custody without bail. The attack, carried out with two planted bombs, injured two law enforcement officers.

stories.title: War as a Force of Destruction, Change, and Opportunity
stories.summary: The Ukraine Compass, a weekly digest published by War on the Rocks, curates Ukrainian media commentary and analysis on the war and its effects. The series aims to present how Ukrainians themselves debate issues of politics, daily life, and public discourse during the conflict.

stories.title: Iran arrests 466 people accused of online activity undermining national security: report
stories.summary: Iranian authorities arrested 466 people accused of online activity deemed a threat to national security. Iranian media reported over 1,000 total arrests in the past month, targeting individuals accused of filming sensitive locations, sharing anti-government content, or cooperating with foreign adversaries.

stories.title: Bangladesh's influential former army general arrested
stories.summary: Bangladeshi police in plain clothes arrested retired Lieutenant General Masud Uddin Chowdhury. He was a key figure in the 2007 government change that installed an interim administration, which governed Bangladesh until elections were held in 2008.

stories.title: In Dnipro, injury toll after Russian attack climbs to 13, including three children
stories.summary: The injury toll from a Russian attack on the city of Dnipro has risen to 13, including three children, according to local authorities.

stories.title: North Korea head uses US 'aggression' to justify nuclear arsenal
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has cited what he describes as US and Israeli aggression in the region to justify his country's nuclear weapons program. Kim has also publicly spoken out against the ongoing war involving Iran.

stories.title: Central Africa: UAE and CEMAC - A Gradually Expanding Economic Partnership
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates is gradually expanding its economic partnership with the Central African Economic and Monetary Community (CEMAC), a bloc traditionally aligned with France, China, the United States, and the European Union. Shifts in the global political economy are enabling emerging actors like the UAE to increase their presence across Central Africa in areas such as infrastructure, finance, and trade.

stories.title: Hong Kong to meet uncertainty with openness, John Lee tells Boao Forum for Asia
stories.summary: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu addressed the Boao Forum for Asia in Hainan, pledging that Hong Kong would respond to rising geopolitical tensions with openness rather than isolation. Lee called on economies to unite in promoting free trade and praised China's commitment to multilateral trade.

stories.title: Africa: AU Iped Supports South Sudan to Strengthen Education Data Systems Through Emis Reform
stories.summary: The African Union's Pan-African Institute for Education for Development held a three-day workshop in Juba to help South Sudan strengthen its Education Management Information System, supported by the GPE Knowledge and Innovation Exchange.

stories.title: China alleges Tokyo embassy break-in, protests to Japan
stories.summary: China has formally protested to Japan over an alleged break-in at its embassy in Tokyo. A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said Beijing was "deeply shocked" by the incident and urged Japan to conduct a thorough investigation, punish those responsible, and provide an explanation.

stories.title: Sadapay says app unavailable after Amazon Web Services disrupted in Bahrain amid war on Iran
stories.summary: Pakistani fintech company Sadapay reported that its mobile application became unavailable to all users after Amazon Web Services infrastructure in Bahrain was disrupted. The company attributed the outage to the impact of the US-Israel conflict with Iran, which has affected services and infrastructure in Gulf countries including Bahrain.

stories.title: Can Lebanon Survive the Digital War?
stories.summary: The article examines Israel's digital warfare tactics against Lebanon, including surveillance technology and online disinformation campaigns, and argues that responding to these threats is essential for Lebanon's survival.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopian Airlines to Lease Two Next-Generation Converted Freighters From Aercap
stories.summary: Ethiopian Airlines agreed to lease two Boeing 777-300ER converted freighters from AerCap Holdings, marking the first introduction of this aircraft type in Africa.

stories.title: U.S. social media addiction trial jury struggles for consensus
stories.summary: A jury in a U.S. social media addiction trial informed Judge Carolyn Kuhl that it was struggling to reach consensus regarding one defendant and sought guidance on how to proceed.

stories.title: In Beirut, refugees stay put despite Israeli strikes
stories.summary: In the southern suburbs of Beirut, Israeli strikes have become a daily occurrence since the start of the wider Middle East conflict, displacing over one million people across Lebanon. Despite the danger, many refugees in the affected neighborhoods have chosen to remain rather than relocate again.

stories.title: Afghanistan announces release of detained US citizen
stories.summary: The Afghan Taliban government announced the release of detained US citizen Dennis Coyle, saying the decision was made in response to a request from his mother.

stories.title: 'We do not have a single war on Iran: We have an Israeli war and an American war'
stories.summary: Professor Scott Lucas of University College Dublin argued that the US-Israel conflict with Iran consists of two distinct wars with diverging objectives. He warned that no diplomatic breakthrough has occurred, and that expectations that escalation will produce Iranian capitulation misunderstand the resilience of Iran's political system.

stories.title: Israel and US interests diverge on possible negociation for end of war
stories.summary: While U.S. President Donald Trump has expressed optimism about negotiating an end to the war with Iran, Israel appears determined to continue military operations. Analysts note that a potential US withdrawal from the conflict would pose significant risks to Israel's strategic objectives.

stories.title: Several wounded in central Israel Iranian missile barrage, one killed from Hezbollah rocket attack
stories.summary: Several people were wounded in central Israel during an Iranian missile barrage, and a woman in her 30s was killed in northern Israel by Hezbollah rocket fire from Lebanon. Two others sustained minor injuries from shattered glass.

stories.title: Alfyorov: Polish order on Ukrainian online auction is provocation with Russian ties
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials allege that the appearance of a Polish Virtuti Militari Order on a Ukrainian collectors' website is a Russian-linked provocation aimed at undermining the Ukrainian-Polish partnership through disinformation.

stories.title: Iranian ballistic missiles kill six Peshmerga in Iraq's Erbil
stories.summary: Iranian ballistic missiles struck a Peshmerga base in Iraq's Erbil province, killing six Peshmerga fighters and wounding dozens, escalating regional tensions.

stories.title: K-Electric appoints Syed Taha as new CEO, replacing interim head
stories.summary: K-Electric appointed Syed Taha, the outgoing CEO of Pakistan State Oil, as its new chief executive officer, replacing interim head Adeeb Ahmad, effective April 15.

stories.title: What to know about the sweeping new EU-Australia trade agreement
stories.summary: The European Union and Australia finalized a long-awaited free-trade agreement on Tuesday as the EU seeks to diversify export markets. European farmers' groups criticized concessions on Australian beef, sugar, and lamb exports as unacceptable.

stories.title: Northern Metropolis boundary changes will need Legco approval, minister says
stories.summary: Hong Kong's development minister confirmed that boundary changes for the Northern Metropolis megaproject near the mainland China border would require Legislative Council approval. The clarification addressed concerns about proposed laws designed to fast-track the large-scale development scheme.

stories.title: DR Congo plans to conduct second national census after 40 years
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo is preparing to conduct its second-ever national census, more than 40 years after the first was held in 1984. The exercise aims to update population data for governance and planning.

stories.title: ‘Persona non grata’: Lebanon boots Iran’s ambassador amid Hezbollah-Israel war
stories.summary: Lebanon expelled Iran's ambassador amid the ongoing Hezbollah-Israel conflict. Israeli Foreign Minister Sa'ar praised the move, while Hezbollah condemned the expulsion. Hours later, an Iranian missile was intercepted over Lebanese territory.

stories.title: Australia, European Union agree sweeping new trade pact 8 years in the works
stories.summary: The European Union and Australia finalized a free-trade agreement after eight years of negotiations, also agreeing to boost defense cooperation and access to rare-earth minerals. EU chief Ursula von der Leyen visited Australia as both sides face energy vulnerability linked to the U.S.-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Mesh networked ‘smart mines’ under development by Poland, Estonia, Ukraine
stories.summary: Poland, Estonia, and Ukraine are jointly developing mesh-networked 'smart mines' designed for deployment along borders with Russia and its allies.

stories.title: Al Jazeera crew 'harassed' while covering arson attack in London
stories.summary: An Al Jazeera news crew was harassed while covering an arson attack in London. Video footage shows the journalists confronted by a group of men chanting "Al Jazeera off our streets" and accusing them of antisemitism.

stories.title: IMF plans Mozambique visit as debt pressures deepen
stories.summary: Mozambique is set to host an International Monetary Fund mission in the coming months as the country faces growing financial pressures. Authorities are seeking IMF support to manage deepening debt challenges.

stories.title: China foreign minister tells Iran counterpart 'talks better than fighting'
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi that "talking is always better than to keep fighting," urging all parties to seize opportunities for peace talks after Tehran denied Trump's claims that negotiations had occurred.

stories.title: Sudan hospital attack toll rises to 70: WHO
stories.summary: The World Health Organization reported that the death toll from a hospital strike in East Darfur, Sudan, has risen to 70, condemning the attack as devastating for civilians caught in Sudan's ongoing war.

stories.title: Are efforts to broker peace deal between Iran and US doomed to fail?
stories.summary: Chinese analysts said backchannel talks between the United States and Iran were unlikely to produce an imminent breakthrough, as core ceasefire conditions remained unmet. President Trump described an unspecified Iranian concession involving the Strait of Hormuz as a "very big present" but provided no details.

stories.title: Israeli press review: Expanding wars spark concerns over economy and air defence capacities
stories.summary: Israeli media report growing concerns about the economic toll of expanding wars and the strain on air defense capacity. Separately, Israel's Knesset approved a controversial law expanding the powers of religious courts.

stories.title: Philippines declares energy emergency over Iran conflict
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. declared an energy emergency, citing "imminent danger" to the country's energy supplies caused by the conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: Russians destroy building of Hetman National Park in Sumy region
stories.summary: Russian shelling destroyed the building of Hetman National Nature Park in the settlement of Velyka Pysarivka in Ukraine's Sumy region.

stories.title: Certain death, small chance of success: The pre-state parachuters who jumped into Nazi Europe
stories.summary: Matti Friedman's new book "Out of the Sky" tells the story of pre-state Jewish parachutists who served as British intelligence operatives and jumped into Nazi-occupied Europe, becoming Zionist heroes despite largely failing their original missions.

stories.title: Albanese urges ICC arrest warrants for Israeli ministers over torture of Palestinians
stories.summary: UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese urged the International Criminal Court to issue arrest warrants for Israeli ministers Ben Gvir, Smotrich, and Katz, accusing them of responsibility for the "systematic torture" of Palestinians.

stories.title: Air Force seeks industry feedback to ‘benchmark’ progress of Northrop missile
stories.summary: The US Air Force is soliciting industry feedback to evaluate the progress of Northrop Grumman's Stand-in Attack Weapon (SiAW) missile. The service indicated it may consider producing an alternative munition if industry can offer faster and cheaper delivery options.

stories.title: Hong Kong bookstore owner, 3 staff held for selling Jimmy Lai biography
stories.summary: Hong Kong police arrested Pong Yat-ming, founder of independent bookstore Book Punch in Sham Shui Po, along with three staff members for selling a biography of jailed media boss Jimmy Lai and other publications deemed seditious. They face charges under the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance.

stories.title: In Iran, hope gives way to fear as conflict rages on
stories.summary: Nearly a month after U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran began, many Iranians who initially hoped the regime would collapse report growing disappointment. Residents told DW that the government's survival has replaced early optimism with fear.

stories.title: Rosneft’s classified document recommended smoke screens against GPS-guided drones — and the same document explains why that’s useless
stories.summary: A leaked classified Rosneft document recommended smoke screens to defend against GPS-guided Ukrainian drones but acknowledged the measures do not guarantee protection. The document also noted structural shortcuts to avoid permit requirements, undermining the defenses' reliability. A concurrent Russian law arming private military companies signals Moscow's recognition that engineering fixes are insufficient.

stories.title: Danish PM seeking third term as election underway
stories.summary: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen sought a third term in elections held on March 24, having called the vote months early amid the Greenland crisis with the United States. However, the campaign was dominated by domestic issues rather than Denmark's relationship with the Trump administration.

stories.title: Who is the new US homeland security chief Markwayne Mullin?
stories.summary: The U.S. Senate confirmed Oklahoma Senator Markwayne Mullin as the new Secretary of Homeland Security in a 54-to-45 vote. He replaces Kristi Noem, who was dismissed earlier in March, and takes charge of an agency central to the Trump administration's immigration enforcement agenda.

stories.title: US-Israel war on Iran 'breach of international law': Steinmeier
stories.summary: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier called the US-Israeli war on Iran a breach of international law and warned of a "deep rift" developing between Germany and the United States.

stories.title: Israel's occupation of South Lebanon 'way to pressure Lebanese government' over Hezbollah
stories.summary: The Israeli Defence Forces announced the establishment of a military zone in southern Lebanon extending approximately 30 kilometres from the border to the Litani River. The IDF said it destroyed a bridge across the river that Hezbollah allegedly used for transferring weapons, rockets, and launchers.

stories.title: Fraught Financing Will Further Weaken the Defense Industrial Base
stories.summary: The Pentagon has proposed a $200 billion private equity fund intended to bolster the defense industrial base. Critics argue the financing approach could ultimately weaken the critical industries it is designed to support.

stories.title: Injury toll after massive Russian shelling in Poltava region rises to 12
stories.summary: The number of people injured in a massive Russian shelling attack in Ukraine's Poltava region has risen to 12, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Chinese corvette recently trained its weapons on Philippine frigate, officials confirm
stories.summary: Philippine officials confirmed that a Chinese corvette trained its weapons on a Philippine Navy frigate during an incident at sea in early March. Officials described the provocation as part of a pattern of Chinese actions designed to tempt sailors into escalatory responses.

stories.title: Qatar national gas company declares force majeure ⁠on some of its long-term LNG supply contracts
stories.summary: QatarEnergy declared force majeure on several long-term LNG supply contracts affecting customers in Italy, Belgium, South Korea, and China, following Iran's attack on the Ras Laffan production facility.

stories.title: Russian Aerospace Company Launches First Batch of Starlink Rival Satellites
stories.summary: A Russian aerospace company has launched its first batch of satellites for the Rassvet constellation, intended to provide broadband internet access across Russia. The system is designed as a domestic alternative to SpaceX's Starlink.

stories.title: China maps ocean floor as it prepares for submarine warfare with US
stories.summary: Dozens of Chinese research vessels are mapping the ocean floor in strategically vital regions worldwide. The effort is part of China's preparations for potential submarine warfare against the United States, aiming to gain underwater domain awareness.

stories.title: Tai Po fire hearing: government rejects assertions surveyors, contractor conspired
stories.summary: A Hong Kong government lawyer rejected claims that government surveyors conspired with a renovation contractor to conceal flammable materials at the site linked to the deadly Tai Po fire. However, the lawyer acknowledged the need for authorities to review supervision of minor construction works and complaint handling.

stories.title: Taking Ukraine’s lessons seriously, Netherlands becomes first NATO member to integrate drones across all combat formations
stories.summary: The Netherlands has become the first NATO member to integrate drone units across all combat formations, applying lessons from the war in Ukraine. The Dutch military plans to recruit up to 1,200 personnel to staff drone units embedded throughout the army rather than concentrating them in specialist formations.

stories.title: Defense Forces clear Minkivka of enemy forces on Bakhmut-Sloviansk highway
stories.summary: Assault units of Ukraine's Skelya regiment cleared the settlement of Minkivka on the Bakhmut-Sloviansk highway of Russian forces, destroying over 40 enemy combatants in the operation.

stories.title: Who is Trump talking to in Iran?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has postponed a threatened bombing of Iran's energy infrastructure, claiming Tehran wants to negotiate a deal with Washington. The diplomatic shift raises questions about back-channel communications between the two countries.

stories.title: Iran war shows why Europe is no longer relevant
stories.summary: The article argues that the US-Israeli war on Iran demonstrates Europe's diminishing geopolitical relevance and further undermines the concept of a rules-based international order.

stories.title: China’s WeRide eyes Hong Kong, Singapore roads for robotaxis as self-driving giants expand
stories.summary: Chinese autonomous-driving company WeRide plans to launch robotaxi and robobus services in Hong Kong and Singapore this year. The Guangzhou-based firm disclosed the expansion plans at a media briefing but did not specify operation areas or launch dates.

stories.title: US Army to demo first crew-free Black Hawk
stories.summary: The U.S. Army has received an H-60Mx, a Black Hawk helicopter equipped with autonomy systems enabling it to fly without a human crew. The service plans to demonstrate the crew-free aircraft as part of its efforts to integrate autonomous capabilities into rotary-wing aviation.

stories.title: EU delays proposal to permanently ban Russian oil imports
stories.summary: The European Commission delayed a proposal to permanently ban Russian oil imports over Moscow's war in Ukraine, missing the planned April 15 deadline. An EU official said the proposal was not cancelled but postponed due to current geopolitical developments, including major oil supply disruptions from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: What new weapons could a supplemental buy, plus news on the Army’s C5ISR plans
stories.summary: Rep. Rob Wittman and Pentagon officials Jules Hurst and Joseph Welch discussed potential weapons acquisitions through a supplemental budget and the US Army's C5ISR modernization plans during a Breaking Defense podcast appearance.

stories.title: JI chief flays govt for ‘burdening’ common citizen with high petroleum prices
stories.summary: Jamaat-i-Islami chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman criticized the Pakistani government for raising petrol and diesel prices by Rs55 per litre to manage the impact of the U.S.-Israel war on Iran, calling the hikes a burden on citizens.

stories.title: Guardian Essential poll: only a quarter of Australians approve of US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: A Guardian Essential poll found that only 25 percent of Australians approve of the US-Israel war on Iran, and just a third support the Australian government's decision to send military assets and troops to the region. Australians expressed stronger support for forging closer ties with middle powers such as Canada and Japan.

stories.title: Why military base on contested Paracels will be of ‘limited’ value to Beijing
stories.summary: Chinese observers assessed that a new Chinese military base on the contested Paracel Islands in the South China Sea would have limited strategic value for Beijing. The assessment comes amid rising concern over China's land reclamation at Antelope Reef, identified as its most significant such project in roughly a decade.

stories.title: Lithuanian PM: Stray crashed drone hailed from Ukraine
stories.summary: Lithuania's prime minister confirmed that a military drone that crashed near the Belarus border originated from Ukraine and was targeting Russian energy infrastructure. She described the incident as part of a broader security situation.

stories.title: Afghanistan releases detained US citizen after more than a year
stories.summary: Afghanistan's Taliban government released detained U.S. citizen Dennis Coyle, a linguist and researcher held for over a year. The release followed a letter from Coyle's family to the Taliban's supreme leader requesting his freedom ahead of the Eid holiday.

stories.title: World Economic Forum postpones meeting planned in Jeddah
stories.summary: The World Economic Forum postponed a planned meeting in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, citing escalating tensions in the Middle East. Iran's recent strikes have heightened global concerns over energy security and regional stability.

stories.title: Hong Kong a ‘safe harbour’ for family wealth as global tensions rise, officials say
stories.summary: Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po described the city as a stable "safe harbour" for global family wealth amid rising geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainties. He spoke at the Wealth for Good in Hong Kong Summit, noting strain on the international rules-based order.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war: A day‑by‑day rundown of the escalating crisis
stories.summary: A joint U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran, including the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, has escalated into a wider war across West Asia, with Tehran and its allies launching retaliatory strikes against Israel, Gulf states, and U.S. military bases.

stories.title: What Iran Wants From the War
stories.summary: Iran is engaging in coercive bargaining amid rising tensions in the Persian Gulf. The article examines Tehran's strategic objectives as conflict dynamics intensify in the region.

stories.title: Jealous Hongkonger who threatened to burn 6 media newsrooms jailed for 1 year
stories.summary: A former Hong Kong civil servant, Tse Chun-pan, was sentenced to 12 months in prison for threatening to burn down the newsrooms of six media outlets including the South China Morning Post. He had demanded the outlets publish seditious material he created to frame his former girlfriend's husband.

stories.title: Ghana, EU sign first pact to counter West Africa's growing insecurity
stories.summary: Ghana and the European Union signed their first formal defence partnership on Tuesday. The agreement aims to counter growing jihadist violence in West Africa, with Ghana positioning itself as a regional security anchor.

stories.title: LaGuardia pilots raised safety alarms months before deadly runway crash
stories.summary: Pilot safety reports filed through NASA's aviation safety reporting system warned of dangerous close calls at New York's LaGuardia Airport months before Sunday's collision between an airplane and a fire truck. The crash killed two pilots and injured 41 others.

stories.title: Philippines declares energy emergency over Middle East conflict
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos declared a national energy emergency on Tuesday, citing threats to domestic fuel supply and energy stability stemming from the broader Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Chad begins relocation of refugees along its border with Sudan
stories.summary: Chad has begun relocating refugees from areas along its border with Sudan, starting with Ennedi Est Province. Authorities are targeting at least 2,300 refugees, mostly women and children, for relocation.

stories.title: Iran crisis: UN meeting set as Rubio attends G7 talks in France
stories.summary: The UN Human Rights Council is set to discuss Iran's recent strikes in the Gulf region. Separately, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is attending G7 talks in France, where the Iran crisis is also on the agenda.

stories.title: Path ahead for Nepal’s new leadership
stories.summary: Nepal's newly elected leader Balendra Shah and his Rastriya Swatantra Party face the challenge of navigating the West Asia conflict and managing relations with India, China, and the United States after securing a historic electoral mandate.

stories.title: Airlines cancel more flights as West Asia conflict escalates
stories.summary: Airlines have canceled additional flights as the West Asia conflict escalates, leaving tens of thousands of passengers stranded amid severe global air travel disruptions.

stories.title: 7.6 magnitude earthquake strikes near Tonga in the South Pacific Ocean
stories.summary: The U.S. Geological Survey reported a preliminary magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck near Tonga in the South Pacific Ocean on Tuesday.

stories.title: Lebanon declares Iran’s ambassador-designate persona non grata, gives him until Sunday to leave
stories.summary: Lebanon declared Iran's ambassador-designate persona non grata and gave him until Sunday to leave. The decision followed a week of meetings between Lebanese officials and regional leaders affected by Iranian attacks.

stories.title: NATO in talks to bring more Ukrainian know-how to allied air defense
stories.summary: NATO is in discussions to incorporate Ukrainian expertise into allied air-defense systems, with the goal of being able to intercept 95 percent of all air threats.

stories.title: General Dynamics-led team unveils self-driving truck with microwave counter-drone tech
stories.summary: A General Dynamics-led team revealed an autonomous ground vehicle built on a Ford F600 truck platform, integrating Kodiak's self-driving software and Epirus' high-power microwave counter-drone system called Leonidas.

stories.title: Why Beijing is blaming Japanese PM as Tokyo moves to downgrade China ties status
stories.summary: Beijing blamed Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's remarks on Taiwan for worsening China-Japan tensions as Tokyo prepared to downgrade its description of bilateral ties in its annual diplomatic report. China's foreign ministry said Takaichi's comments breached a "red line" and sparked anger in China.

stories.title: Russia marched into Huliaipole in December. Now it can’t march out.
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces have made advances near Huliaipole in southeastern Ukraine, trapping Russian troops that entered the area in December. The gains are reportedly easing military pressure on Zaporizhzhia city and its approximately 700,000 pre-war residents.

stories.title: Pakistan PM says Islamabad ‘ready’ to host talks to end Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced that Islamabad was prepared to host negotiations between the United States and Iran to end the war in the Middle East. He expressed full support for dialogue efforts and said Pakistan stood ready to facilitate talks, subject to agreement from both parties.

stories.title: Gaza marks 'Resistance Against Colonialism and Apartheid' week
stories.summary: Gaza is observing a week-long event titled 'Resistance Against Colonialism and Apartheid,' part of a global initiative launched in 2005. The campaign aims to raise international awareness and expand boycott efforts and political pressure on Israel.

stories.title: ‘Extraordinary event’ for mountain gorillas as new twins born in DRC
stories.summary: A second set of mountain gorilla twins has been born in Virunga National Park in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, just two months after another twin birth was discovered in the park. Conservationists described the rare occurrence as extraordinary for the endangered species.

stories.title: Russia’s biggest oil company can’t stop Ukraine’s drones – a leaked report shows what it’s trying instead
stories.summary: A leaked internal report from Rosneft, Russia's largest oil company, reveals that its engineers acknowledge existing defenses against Ukrainian drone strikes do not guarantee the safety of protected facilities and cannot prevent blast damage.

stories.title: Anger in Cyprus as Iran war spotlights 'colonial' UK bases
stories.summary: A drone incident in early March has reignited debate in Cyprus over the future of British sovereign military bases on the island. Cypriot officials are calling for a frank discussion about the bases amid the wider Iran conflict.

stories.title: Why Ukraine’s Cabinet drafted a resolution to fire its anti-corruption chief—and why it never came to a vote?
stories.summary: Ukraine's Cabinet drafted a resolution to dismiss the head of the National Anti-Corruption Bureau, but the measure never came to a vote. The effort reportedly involved a secret audit draft, smear campaigns, and blame-shifting tactics targeting the bureau.

stories.title: Hotels become lifeline for Iranians fleeing US-Israel airstrikes
stories.summary: Hotels across Iran have become emergency shelters for thousands of civilians fleeing US-Israeli airstrikes. Overcrowding and insufficient humanitarian support are leaving displaced families in dire conditions.

stories.title: iPhone spyware DarkSword hits Malaysia, exposing spread of sophisticated hacking tools
stories.summary: Malaysian iPhone users were among those targeted by newly uncovered spyware called DarkSword, which also hit entities in Ukraine, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey. Researchers said multiple threat actors deployed the sophisticated mobile-hacking tool, indicating the spread of such capabilities through commercial and criminal networks.

stories.title: Iran sends waves of missiles into Israel, dismisses Trump's talk of negotiations as 'fake news'
stories.summary: Iran launched waves of missiles into Israel, triggering air raid sirens across the country including Tel Aviv. Homes in northern Israel were damaged by falling debris from interceptions, though no deaths were reported. Tehran dismissed U.S. President Trump's talk of negotiations as "fake news."

stories.title: St. Petersburg Judge Sentences Oxxxymiron to Community Service in Absentia for ‘Foreign Agent’ Violations
stories.summary: A St. Petersburg court sentenced exiled rapper Oxxxymiron to community service in absentia for violating Russia's "foreign agent" labeling requirements. Russia had previously issued an arrest warrant after he was accused of repeatedly failing to include the mandatory disclaimer on his Telegram posts.

stories.title: Belgorod Region to Use Armored Vehicles for Food Deliveries in Drone-Struck Border Areas
stories.summary: Authorities in Russia's Belgorod region announced plans to use armored vehicles for food deliveries in border areas frequently hit by drone strikes. Governor Vyacheslav Gladkov compared the logistics effort to a "military operation."

stories.title: Israel bombs Tehran as Iran hits Telaviv, Gulf states
stories.summary: Israel carried out extensive strikes on Iranian targets it described as production sites, while Iran fired multiple waves of missiles at Israel and Gulf states. Both Tehran and Tel Aviv sustained direct hits in the exchange.

stories.title: 'Night of terror' in Lebanon as Israel escalates Beirut assault
stories.summary: Israel has intensified its military assault across Lebanon, including strikes on Beirut. Israeli officials have threatened to expand control northward to the Litani River, raising fears of a deeper ground invasion.

stories.title: Japan to start release of state oil reserve on Thursday to ease Iran impact
stories.summary: Japan announced it would begin releasing 30 days' worth of state oil reserves starting Thursday to cushion economic impacts from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The government plans to sell approximately 8.5 million kilolitres from 11 storage bases nationwide, following the private sector's release of 15 days' worth of stockpiles last week.

stories.title: Watch: ‘Unacceptable’: EU President slams Iran for Strait of Hormuz tensions
stories.summary: European Union President condemned Iran over escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, calling the situation unacceptable.

stories.title: US-Israel strikes, Gulf attacks continue amid confusion on talks
stories.summary: Iran reported that several gas installations were struck despite US President Donald Trump's claim that such attacks would be paused for five days. The contradictory statements have fueled confusion over the status of any diplomatic talks.

stories.title: Swiss Destinus, Shield AI wrap European drone autonomy test campaign
stories.summary: Swiss company Destinus and US-based Shield AI completed a joint drone autonomy test campaign in Europe. The firms are marketing the demonstration to European air forces seeking counter-UAS solutions that reduce dependence on crewed aircraft, though no customers have signed on yet.

stories.title: Iran replaces slain security chief with IRGC hardliner
stories.summary: Iran appointed Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, a former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander, as the new chief of the Supreme National Security Council. He replaces a security official who was recently killed.

stories.title: Why DHL is betting on rising Chinese exports – even as war and tariff risks grow
stories.summary: Logistics giant DHL expects revenues to rise in coming years despite disruptions from the U.S.-Israel war on Iran and shifting tariff policies, largely due to Chinese companies' growing global trade ambitions. CEO Oscar de Bok cited the resilience of China's outbound trade as a major factor in maintaining ambitious growth targets.

stories.title: Silence not an option, says Canadian Sikh activist Moninder Singh after fresh threats
stories.summary: Canadian Sikh activist Moninder Singh spoke at the UN's European headquarters in Geneva after receiving assassination threats against his family. He called for international action against India's alleged targeting of Sikh activists abroad.

stories.title: Moldova Accuses Russia of Damaging Key Power Line Connecting It With Romania
stories.summary: Moldova accused Russia of damaging the Issacea-Vulcanesti power line connecting it to Romania. The Moldovan government said the damage resulted from overnight Russian strikes on southern Ukraine.

stories.title: At least 66 killed in military plane crash in Colombia
stories.summary: A military plane crash in Colombia killed at least 66 people. General Hugo Alejandro Lopez Barreto confirmed that four military personnel remained missing following the incident.

stories.title: Ukraine hits Bastion missile launcher in occupied Crimea used to fire Onyx missiles at Ukrainian cities
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck a P-800 Onyx-capable Bastion coastal missile launcher overnight on 24 March in the occupied Crimean village of Aktachi. The launcher had been used to fire Onyx missiles at Ukrainian cities.

stories.title: Lebanon withdraws Iran envoy's accreditation, orders to leave
stories.summary: Lebanon has withdrawn the accreditation of Iran's ambassador and declared him persona non grata. Lebanese authorities have demanded that the Iranian envoy leave the country by Sunday.

stories.title: Rising fuel prices and Middle East tensions hit South African Airlines
stories.summary: South African airlines face mounting operational pressures as jet fuel prices have surged more than 70 percent since late February. The increases are driven by ongoing instability in the Middle East disrupting global energy markets.

stories.title: WatchNetanyahu says Trump sees chance of striking deal with Iran
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that U.S. President Donald Trump sees a potential opportunity to strike a deal with Iran.

stories.title: Israel evicts Palestinians in West Bank amid settler attacks
stories.summary: Israeli settler violence in the West Bank injured five Palestinians as evictions and demolitions of Palestinian homes surged across the occupied territory.

stories.title: Szijjártó confirms Lavrov calls, denies security breach
stories.summary: Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó confirmed at a campaign rally that he regularly contacts Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov before and after closed EU Council sessions. Szijjártó characterized the calls as routine diplomacy and denied any security breach.

stories.title: Kim vows to ’irreversibly’ cement North Korea’s nuclear status, calls South ’most hostile’
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un pledged to irreversibly cement the country's nuclear status and designated South Korea as the "most hostile" state. Analysts say Kim views Seoul as an obstacle to his push for a more assertive regional role rather than a useful intermediary with Washington.

stories.title: Lithuanian PM confirms Ukrainian drone crashed on Lithuanian territory
stories.summary: Lithuanian Prime Minister confirmed that a Ukrainian strike drone crashed on Lithuanian territory after an attack on Russia's Primorsk oil terminal. The drone veered off course and landed in Lithuania.

stories.title: Nigeria: Iran War May Push Nigerians to Work From Home - Dangote
stories.summary: Dangote Group president Aliko Dangote warned that escalating Middle East tensions linked to the Iran conflict could force Nigeria and other African nations to adopt pandemic-style work-from-home measures.

stories.title: Why Vietnam is leaning on Russia to weather energy turmoil
stories.summary: Vietnam is turning to Russia for energy deals as the global energy crisis caused by the Iran war hits Southeast Asian economies hard. Vietnamese Prime Minister Pham Minh Chinh visited Russia this week and reportedly signed several energy agreements as Hanoi seeks to maintain its double-digit economic growth target.

stories.title: Chances of US-Iran deal 'very small,' Israeli officials tell 'Post'
stories.summary: Israeli officials told the Jerusalem Post that the chances of a US-Iran deal remain very small. American and Israeli sources confirmed that military strikes are continuing as planned with no changes in coordination.

stories.title: Paris Fashion Week 2026: WforWoman marks India’s first high-street showcase
stories.summary: Indian high-street fashion brand WforWoman debuted at Paris Fashion Week 2026, marking India's first high-street showcase at the event. The collection blended vintage European aesthetics with Indian textile craftsmanship.

stories.title: China warns Japan that ‘new militarism’, ‘Takaichinomics’ risk instability
stories.summary: China's People's Daily warned Japan that increased military spending and what it termed "Takaichinomics" risk instability. The commentary, published under the "Zhong Sheng" pen name used for official foreign policy positions, said higher defense budgets would not rescue Japan's economy amid the falling yen and energy crisis.

stories.title: Senior Chinese financial regulator and ex-graft fighter Zhou Liang under corruption probe
stories.summary: Zhou Liang, vice-chairman of China's National Financial Regulatory Administration and a former anti-corruption official, was placed under investigation for "serious violations of discipline and law." The probe marks one of the highest-profile purges within China's financial regulatory system in recent years.

stories.title: Nigeria: Brain Drain - Improve Remuneration, Fix Naira and Doctors Will Stay - - Prof Ebeigbe
stories.summary: Data from Nigeria's Medical and Dental Council shows that in 2024, roughly 4,200 of about 4,900 newly registered doctors sought certificates to practice abroad. Professor Ebeigbe called for improved pay and a stabilized naira to retain medical professionals.

stories.title: Pakistan ranked most polluted country in 2025, data shows
stories.summary: Pakistan was ranked the world's most polluted country in 2025 by Swiss firm IQAir, with PM2.5 concentrations up to 13 times higher than WHO-recommended levels. Overall, 130 of 143 monitored countries failed to meet WHO air quality guidelines.

stories.title: Deadly strikes in Iraq blamed on US and Iran
stories.summary: Deadly strikes in Iraq killed 15 paramilitary fighters and six Kurdish security personnel. The attacks have been attributed to both US and Iranian forces as the Iran conflict continues to spill into neighboring countries.

stories.title: Kenya Airways sees surge in demand as Middle East conflict disrupts global travel
stories.summary: Kenya Airways reports a sharp surge in flight bookings in recent weeks as the Middle East conflict disrupts global travel patterns. The airline is benefiting from passengers seeking alternative routes.

stories.title: Elon Musk's Starlink blocked from operating in Namibia
stories.summary: Namibia's telecommunications regulator has blocked Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet service from operating in the country. The regulator cited the fact that Starlink's local subsidiary does not meet local ownership requirements.

stories.title: Munition Remnants Pictured at Site of Deadly Chad Strike Match Weapon Previously Used by Sudan’s RSF
stories.summary: Munition remnants found at the site of a strike that killed at least 17 people in Tiné, Chad, match a weapon previously used by Sudan's Rapid Support Forces. The RSF denied involvement, but photographic evidence analyzed by Bellingcat links the munitions to the paramilitary group.

stories.title: Visiting galleries may keep artworks in Hong Kong for months due to shipping chaos
stories.summary: Overseas galleries exhibiting at Art Central in Hong Kong are considering keeping artworks in the city for months due to shipping disruptions from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. Gallerists reported fuel surcharges for shipping to Hong Kong had increased up to fourfold ahead of the fair's opening at the Central Harbourfront.

stories.title: Ukraine wants to import gas from Mozambique, Zelensky says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky proposed importing gas from Mozambique following a meeting with his Mozambican counterpart. In exchange, Ukraine offered assistance with Mozambique's security challenges.

stories.title: Nigeria: Boat Mishap - Nigerian Navy Rescues Seven Survivors in Bayelsa
stories.summary: The Nigerian Navy rescued seven survivors after a boat collision in the waterways of Bayelsa State in southeastern Nigeria.

stories.title: South Africa: A R60 Test Could Help South Africa Find Millions More TB Patients - But Will It Miss The Most Dangerous Cases?
stories.summary: South Africa is trialling a portable tuberculosis test costing about R60, roughly one-third of the current standard. However, the new test cannot detect drug-resistant TB, raising concerns about diagnostic trade-offs.

stories.title: Lessons for Singapore From Trump’s War in Iran
stories.summary: The article analyzes lessons for Singapore drawn from the U.S. war with Iran. It highlights how Singapore's strategic geographic location and close partnership with the United States could make it an attractive military target in a broader conflict.

stories.title: Memory costs ‘beyond imagination’ may imperil smartphone makers, Xiaomi leader warns
stories.summary: Xiaomi president William Lu Weibing warned that surging memory-chip costs at a magnitude "beyond imagination" could reshape the smartphone industry. He cautioned that a prolonged price-raising cycle could cause some manufacturers to suffer significant losses or face closure.

stories.title: South Africa: How a Boy Born on World TB Day Helped Turn the Tide on South Africa's Deadliest TB
stories.summary: A profile of Norbert Ndjeka, born on World TB Day, highlights his decades-long role in reshaping South Africa's treatment of the deadliest forms of tuberculosis.

stories.title: Iran hits Israel with missiles after denying Trump talks
stories.summary: Iran launched a new missile barrage targeting Tel Aviv, causing damage and injuries in Israel. The attack came after Tehran denied participating in any US-led negotiations to de-escalate the conflict.

stories.title: Libya: Libya's $210m Investment in Sandton Yields Zero Benefits for the North African Nation's People
stories.summary: Libya's roughly $210 million investment in The Michelangelo Hotel and other Sandton, South Africa, properties has reportedly yielded no returns for Libyan citizens over two decades due to mismanagement and legal disputes.

stories.title: Rwanda: Surrounded and Outnumbered - Why Resistance Failed During the Genocide
stories.summary: An analysis from Rwanda's New Times examines how the organized structure behind the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi enabled the massacres to reach devastating levels.

stories.title: Large oil refinery explosion near Texas coast forces residents to shelter in place
stories.summary: An explosion occurred at the Valero oil refinery in Port Arthur, Texas, prompting authorities to order nearby residents to shelter in place. Port Arthur Mayor Charlotte M. Moses confirmed no injuries resulted from the blast.

stories.title: Argentina marches on 50th anniversary of coup that led to the Falklands War and the regime's fall
stories.summary: Thousands gathered in Plaza de Mayo and other major Argentine cities on the 50th anniversary of the March 24, 1976, military coup. The dictatorship was responsible for thousands of forced disappearances and ultimately launched the Falklands War in a failed attempt to retain power.

stories.title: New Type 055 destroyers for PLA East China Fleet tested in first live-fire drill
stories.summary: Two newly commissioned Type 055 guided-missile destroyers, the Dongguan and Anqing, conducted their first live-fire training exercise in mid-March after being assigned to the PLA East China Fleet division overseeing Taiwan and the East China Sea. The 12,000-tonne warships simulated high-intensity combat missions during the drill.

stories.title: The ‘simple maneuver’ of opening Hormuz strait carries great risks, analysts say
stories.summary: Analysts warn that reopening the Strait of Hormuz carries significant risks despite President Trump's characterization of the operation as simple. Issue experts say the economically vital passage presents complex military and strategic challenges.

stories.title: US journalists sue to protect Voice of America from political control
stories.summary: Voice of America journalists filed a lawsuit in Washington, D.C., accusing the Trump administration of undermining the broadcaster's editorial independence and turning its transmissions to Iran, China, and other regions into vehicles for political messaging.

stories.title: Iranian Military Branch Casts Shadow Across Africa
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has been expanding its influence across the African continent, engaging with various state and non-state actors to extend Tehran's strategic reach beyond the Middle East.

stories.title: La rama militar iraní proyecta su sombra sobre África
stories.summary: La rama militar de Irán, el Cuerpo de la Guardia Revolucionaria Islámica, ha estado ampliando su presencia e influencia en varios países africanos, proyectando el alcance estratégico de Teherán en el continente.

stories.title: Ramo militar iraniano lança sua sombra sobre a África
stories.summary: O Corpo da Guarda Revolucionária Islâmica do Irã tem expandido sua presença em países africanos, ampliando a influência estratégica de Teerã no continente por meio de parcerias com atores estatais e não estatais.

stories.title: Iran’s Minorities Will Pay the Price for Trump’s War
stories.summary: Iran's ethnic and religious minorities face heightened repression as the regime seeks scapegoats amid the ongoing war. The battered Iranian government is directing blame inward as it contends with external military pressure from the United States and Israel.

stories.title: China coach goes above and beyond, trains clients at own cost of US$28,000 after gym shuts
stories.summary: A fitness coach surnamed Zhang in Wuhan, Hubei province, spent 200,000 yuan (US$28,000) of his own money to complete 877 classes for clients after Aishang Gym suddenly closed without issuing refunds. The story went viral on Chinese social media, receiving half a million likes.

stories.title: UN warns of systematic abuse in Occupied Palestinian Territories
stories.summary: The United Nations has raised serious concerns about conditions in the Palestinian territories occupied since 1967. Officials warned that abuse of Palestinians appears to be deliberate, widespread, and systematic.

stories.title: Liberia: Boakai Seeks France's Intervention As Guinean Troops, Customs Officers Deploy On Liberian Soil
stories.summary: Liberian President Joseph Boakai reportedly contacted French President Emmanuel Macron seeking France's intervention in a border dispute with Guinea after Guinean troops and customs officers deployed on Liberian soil.

stories.title: Kenya: Kenya Flags Off First Exports to China Under Zero-Tariff Agreement
stories.summary: Kenya dispatched its first consignment of exports to China under a newly implemented zero-tariff arrangement, a step officials say could help narrow the bilateral trade imbalance.

stories.title: Gold down 27%, Urals up 71%—Russia’s sanctions hedge melts as its oil budget fills
stories.summary: Russia's gold reserves have declined by 27 percent while revenues from Urals crude oil have risen by 71 percent. The shift indicates that Moscow's sanctions hedge is eroding even as wartime oil income fills its budget.

stories.title: Inside a Beijing lab, humanoid robots are put to the test
stories.summary: Engineers at X-Humanoid, a robotics company in Beijing, are conducting eight-hour endurance tests on humanoid robots. The tests evaluate the robots' coordination, agility, and motor skills as they walk, run, and dance.

stories.title: Trump sends mixed signals on Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump sent mixed signals regarding his administration's approach to Iran amid ongoing tensions.

stories.title: Trump announces ‘very good’ Iran talks denied by Tehran
stories.summary: President Trump announced what he called "very good" talks with Iran, a claim Tehran denied. U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner may meet an Iranian delegation in Pakistan as soon as this week, with Vice President J.D. Vance possibly joining the discussions.

stories.title: China EV makers gain as Iran war drives up fuel costs
stories.summary: Chinese petrol prices rose by 1,160 yuan per tonne and diesel by 1,115 yuan, the largest increases since 2000, driven by the war in Iran disrupting global oil markets. The NDRC said increases would have been double without government intervention. Chinese electric vehicle makers are benefiting from the surge in fuel costs.

stories.title: Zimbabwe opposition leader granted bail amid growing tensions over constitutional changes
stories.summary: Zimbabwean opposition leader Tendai Biti was granted bail after being detained over the weekend. He was arrested near the Mozambique border alongside an activist, accused of holding a public meeting without notifying authorities.

stories.title: During NATO exercises in Romania, troops are training to repel a Russian attack in the Black Sea
stories.summary: NATO is conducting its largest Black Sea naval exercise of the year in Romania, involving more than 2,500 troops from 12 allied nations. The drills focus on repelling a potential Russian attack, as sea mines continue to pose weekly threats in the waterway.

stories.title: Iran says Trump talks 'fake news' aimed at oil market influence
stories.summary: Iran dismissed US President Donald Trump's claims that negotiations between Washington and Tehran were underway. Iranian officials called the remarks 'fake news' intended to manipulate global oil markets.

stories.title: How Iran’s Deterrence Collapsed Ahead of the War
stories.summary: The article examines how Iran's deterrence strategy collapsed prior to the U.S.-Israeli military campaign. A key failure in 2024 is identified as having paved the way for the attacks that followed.

stories.title: How the US, Israel & Iran are controlling their media narratives
stories.summary: An analysis by Majdoline Al-Shammouri argues that the United States, Israel, and Iran are all engaging in censorship and media repression to shape public perception of the ongoing war.

stories.title: China slams Japan’s ‘kill network’ as long-range missile deployment looms
stories.summary: The People's Liberation Army Daily condemned Japan's planned deployment of upgraded Type-12 surface-to-ship missiles at Camp Kengun in Kumamoto prefecture, accusing Tokyo of creating a "kill network" targeting coastal and inland areas of neighbouring countries. The deployment is expected by the end of the month.

stories.title: Russia knocks out Moldova–Romania power link in strike on Ukraine
stories.summary: Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure on 23 March severed Moldova's primary power link to Romania and the broader European electricity grid.

stories.title: Trump’s energy war over Iran is failing just like his China trade war
stories.summary: The article argues that President Trump's military campaign against Iran, like his trade war with China, is imposing broad costs. Iran has leveraged its control of the Strait of Hormuz, through which 20 per cent of global crude oil flows, to counteract U.S. military pressure.

stories.title: Albanese urged to help Australians struggling with fuel crisis, as NZ offers first-of-its-kind cash relief
stories.summary: Independent Australian senator David Pocock proposed a flat 25 percent export levy on gas producers to redirect profits to households struggling with rising fuel costs. New Zealand announced a weekly cash payment for nearly 150,000 families to help afford petrol amid the Middle East-driven fuel crisis.

stories.title: South Africa: TB Stigma Still Keeps People From Testing and Treatment in South Africa
stories.summary: Tuberculosis remains South Africa's deadliest infectious disease, with 56,000 people dying from it in 2023. Stigma continues to deter many South Africans from seeking testing and treatment.

stories.title: Russia fires 426 missiles and drones at Ukraine overnight — air defense intercepts 92%, but 33 weapons find their mark
stories.summary: Russia launched 426 missiles and drones at Ukraine overnight on 24 March. Ukrainian air defenses intercepted 92 percent, destroying all 23 cruise missiles and 365 of 392 drones, but six missiles and 27 drones struck targets across 11 oblasts.

stories.title: Denmark votes in election shadowed by Trump’s Greenland ambitions
stories.summary: Denmark held a national election on Tuesday, with polls suggesting Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's Social Democrats may secure a third term despite projections of their weakest result since before World War II. Her firm stance against President Trump's ambitions regarding Greenland has bolstered her support, though cost-of-living concerns have eroded her domestic standing.

stories.title: Cathay Pacific extends suspension of flights between Hong Kong, Middle East to end of May
stories.summary: Cathay Pacific Airways extended its suspension of all flights between Hong Kong and the Middle East through the end of May, marking at least the fourth extension since early March. The airline cited the ongoing regional conflict. It plans to increase European flights starting next month to meet surging demand.

stories.title: Egyptian outrage as Ethiopia plans more dams on Blue Nile
stories.summary: Ethiopia announced plans to construct three additional dams on the Blue Nile, to be built within four to seven years. The announcement has provoked outrage in Egypt, which depends heavily on Nile water resources.

stories.title: Singapore says involvement in Israeli military-linked groups ‘not acceptable’
stories.summary: Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Defence warned on Tuesday that involvement in organisations linked to the Israeli military, such as volunteer group Sar-El, is not acceptable under current conditions and could result in legal action. Sar-El's website states its volunteers work alongside Israeli Defence Forces soldiers on military bases.

stories.title: No new cabinet without 'Islamic resistance', Iraqi militia says
stories.summary: Pro-Iranian militias in Iraq have declared that no new cabinet should be formed without the inclusion of the 'Islamic resistance.' The groups are increasingly viewed as undermining Iraqi state institutions to consolidate their own power.

stories.title: Two pilots killed as jet collides with fire truck at New York’s LaGuardia Airport
stories.summary: Two pilots were killed when an Air Canada Express jet collided with a fire truck at LaGuardia Airport in New York. The plane tilted back on its tail on the tarmac, its cockpit smashed, surrounded by emergency vehicles.

stories.title: Japanese ‘military officer’ forces way into Chinese embassy in Tokyo
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said a Japanese individual claiming to be an active Self-Defence Forces officer illegally and forcibly entered the Chinese embassy in Tokyo. The individual reportedly threatened to kill Chinese diplomatic personnel. Beijing lodged a strong protest with Japan over the incident.

stories.title: The Next Transformation of U.S. Shipbuilding
stories.summary: Eric Chewning, executive vice president at HII—America's largest military shipbuilder—discusses the challenges of adopting AI and automation in shipbuilding. The interview covers cultural barriers in legacy shipyards, maritime startups, and reindustrialization policy.

stories.title: Rights to antibody drug from China’s Keymed change hands in Gilead acquisition of Ouro
stories.summary: U.S. biopharmaceutical company Gilead Sciences agreed to acquire Ouro Medicines for up to US$2.18 billion. Ouro is developing an antibody-based autoimmune disease treatment licensed from China's Keymed Biosciences. Gilead will pay Ouro shareholders US$1.675 billion upfront as part of the deal.

stories.title: Netanyahu says spoke with Trump, vows to protect Israel's interests
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he spoke with President Trump and vowed to protect Israel's interests. Netanyahu also claimed Israel recently eliminated two more Iranian nuclear scientists, stating "this is not the end."

stories.title: Converting History into Hard Power: A Polish-German Reckoning
stories.summary: Nearly 70 percent of the Polish public believes Germany has not adequately addressed the destruction it inflicted on Poland during World War II. This unresolved historical grievance is gaining strategic significance as Germany seeks to lead European security and U.S. engagement in Europe becomes less certain.

stories.title: Xi calls for bold innovation drive to build Xiongan, China’s ‘city of the future’
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping inspected the Xiongan New Area in Hebei province on Monday, calling for the development of the state-level megacity into an innovation hub. Located about 100 kilometres southwest of Beijing, Xiongan is Xi's signature urban project designed to relieve pressure on the capital.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Biti's Arrest a Cowardly Act Says Ugandan Opposition Leader Bobi Wine
stories.summary: Ugandan opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi, known as Bobi Wine, condemned the arrest of Zimbabwean former legislator Tendai Biti, accusing the Zimbabwean government of shrinking democratic space.

stories.title: Cuba's mothers-to-be prepare to give birth in a country plunged into darkness
stories.summary: Pregnant women in Cuba are preparing to give birth amid a deepening national crisis. The country faces severe hardship, including widespread power outages, as expectant mothers navigate limited resources.

stories.title: China dials back on fuel price hikes to 'reduce burden' on drivers
stories.summary: China reduced planned fuel price increases to ease the financial burden on drivers amid soaring global fuel costs driven by regional instability.

stories.title: Analysts warn $200 oil is no longer a far-fetched scenario
stories.summary: Energy analysts warn that oil prices could exceed $150 per barrel and approach $200 if the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz continues. Analysts say such price levels would make a global recession virtually inevitable.

stories.title: Why China Is Stoking Division in Myanmar’s Anti-Junta Alliance
stories.summary: China is actively stoking divisions within Myanmar's anti-junta resistance alliance. Beijing's interference is driven by fears that continued instability could produce a failed state along its border.

stories.title: Irish metals refinery is in supply chain that feeds Russian war machine, records suggest
stories.summary: Records suggest that Aughinish Alumina, a Rusal-owned refinery on Ireland's Shannon estuary, is part of an aluminium supply chain that feeds Russian arms producers. Shipments from the Irish facility to Russian smelters have increased sharply since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

stories.title: Japan to begin biggest-ever oil release from national reserves as Middle East energy crisis bites
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced the country's largest-ever release of oil from strategic reserves, totaling approximately 80 million barrels equivalent to 45 days of domestic demand. The move responds to potential supply shortages caused by disrupted tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz due to the conflict involving the US and Israel against Iran.

stories.title: New Zealand to give cash payments to some low income families as global fuel crisis worsens
stories.summary: New Zealand announced that approximately 143,000 families with children will receive an extra NZ$50 per week through a boost to the in-work tax credit beginning April 1. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon and Finance Minister Nicola Willis said the measure addresses surging fuel prices caused by the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Colombian military plane crashes after takeoff with more than 120 people on board
stories.summary: A Colombian Air Force C-130 Hercules crashed shortly after takeoff from La Tagua airstrip in Puerto Leguízamo, Putumayo, in southern Colombia. The aircraft was carrying at least 125 people, including troops on a routine rotation to Puerto Asís.

stories.title: Dollar falls and São Paulo stock exchange surges after Trump's truce signal with Iran
stories.summary: Brazilian financial markets surged after U.S. President Donald Trump announced a five-day postponement of strikes on Iran's energy infrastructure, citing productive conversations with Tehran. The Brazilian real strengthened and the São Paulo stock exchange posted one of its best sessions of the year.

stories.title: U.S. military pause on Iran attack: India tracking developments, says Centre
stories.summary: The U.S. military paused its planned attack on Iran, a development India said it was closely tracking. The announcement contributed to a sharp decline in oil prices, with benchmark Brent Crude futures dropping more than 12 percent.

stories.title: Tonga PM welcomes US deal to explore deep-sea minerals amid environmental concerns
stories.summary: Tonga's newly elected Prime Minister Lord Fakafānua welcomed a partnership deal with the United States to explore deep-sea minerals in the South Pacific. Critics have raised concerns about the environmental impact of seabed mining in the region, which holds critical minerals for green technologies.

stories.title: Australia and EU strike free trade deal
stories.summary: The European Union and Australia have finalized a comprehensive free trade agreement. Both sides made compromises to boost exports amid global trade uncertainty.

stories.title: Iran war shows the strategic limits of tactical strikes
stories.summary: Analysts argue the U.S.-led war against Iran demonstrates that tactical military strikes face strategic limits. A complex web of economic and geopolitical consequences is preventing either side from achieving a decisive victory.

stories.title: ‘A miracle’: Canadian flight attendant ejected from plane survives New York crash
stories.summary: A flight attendant on the Air Canada Jazz CRJ-900 that collided with a fire truck at LaGuardia Airport was ejected more than 100 metres from the aircraft while still strapped to her seat and survived. The collision killed two pilots during landing at the New York airport.

stories.title: Milei willing to send troops to the Middle East if requested by Trump
stories.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei has expressed willingness to deploy troops to the Middle East if requested by the United States. The stance has sparked concern in Argentina, which has historically maintained neutrality in international conflicts, with fears of possible reprisals.

stories.title: Eight arrested for ‘brutal’ attack on capybara in Brazil
stories.summary: Police in Rio de Janeiro arrested eight people for brutally beating a capybara, an incident captured on security cameras. The group attacked the animal with sticks and iron bars.

stories.title: Trump delays strikes on Iran's energy grid by five days, claims “productive” talks
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced a five-day moratorium on threatened strikes against Iran's energy infrastructure, hours before a 48-hour ultimatum demanding Tehran reopen the Strait of Hormuz was set to expire. Trump cited what he called productive talks with Iran.

stories.title: Trump claims ‘good and productive’ talks with Iran, which denies negotiating
stories.summary: President Trump claimed "good and productive" talks with Iran and suggested the Strait of Hormuz would come under "joint control," while Iran denied any negotiations were taking place. Trump also characterized removing uranium as "very easy."

stories.title: Inside the alleged Russian operation to trigger anti-government protests in Angola
stories.summary: A group of Russians and Angolans are standing trial in Angola on charges of orchestrating anti-government protests. The defendants deny the accusations of fomenting unrest in the country.

stories.title: ‘We consider every mile we drive’: how fuel shortages are affecting readers worldwide
stories.summary: Rising fuel prices driven by the Middle East conflict are forcing people worldwide to ration fuel usage. In Coimbatore, India, a shop owner faces business closure due to LPG shortages, while communities across multiple countries report similar hardships from disrupted energy supplies.

stories.title: UK universities flock to India - but will they succeed?
stories.summary: Nine UK universities are establishing campuses in India, though initial enrollment is expected to be modest.

stories.title: UK police see antisemitic motive in arson of ambulances
stories.summary: British counterterrorism police are investigating an arson attack on ambulances operated by a Jewish charity in north London. Officers suspect the attack was motivated by antisemitism.

stories.title: Argentina's 'Dirty War' still on trial 50 years later
stories.summary: Argentina continues to prosecute crimes committed during its 1976–1983 military dictatorship, during which an estimated 30,000 people were forcibly disappeared. Victims and their families are still pursuing justice 50 years later.

stories.title: Lebanon PM says Iran Guards commanding Hezbollah operations in Lebanon
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of commanding Hezbollah operations inside Lebanon. Salam criticized Hezbollah for dragging Lebanon into the wider West Asia war by firing rockets at Israel.

stories.title: Pakistan vows to ‘eradicate terrorism’ as Afghan truce nears end
stories.summary: Pakistan vowed to eradicate terrorism as a truce with Afghan forces neared its end. Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar indicated that Islamabad's approach to the conflict remained unchanged.

stories.title: Taiwan opposition leader says talks with Xi a 'bridge' to peace
stories.summary: Taiwan's opposition leader proposed that talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping could serve as a bridge to peace across the Taiwan Strait.

stories.title: North Korea’s Kim reappointed as president of state affairs
stories.summary: North Korea's Kim Jong Un was reappointed as president of state affairs, reaffirming his position atop the country's governing structure.

stories.title: As conflicts intensify in Sudan and South Sudan, fleeing civilians are caught within closed borders
stories.summary: Intensifying conflicts in both Sudan and South Sudan have displaced large numbers of civilians who face closed borders.
