In Sudan, fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces has escalated, while South Sudan nears civil war between government and opposition forces. The crises have become a regional emergency involving mass killings and territorial fragmentation.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1490: Russia threw 600 attacks in 4 days and lost 6,000 troops
stories.summary: Russia launched over 600 attacks along Ukraine's front lines in four days, suffering more than 6,000 troops killed or wounded without breaking through any Ukrainian positions, according to Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi.

stories.title: Washington 20 March 2026 #3
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced a short-term authorization permitting the sale of approximately 140 million barrels of Iranian oil stranded at sea. The move aimed to expand global energy supply and relieve price pressures caused by the disruption of Iranian oil flows.

stories.title: Washington 21 March 2026 #2
stories.summary: President Trump issued a 48-hour ultimatum demanding Iran fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to destroy Iranian power plants if it did not comply. Iran's military responded by warning it would target US and allied energy, IT, and water desalination infrastructure in the region.

stories.title: Tehran 21 March 2026 #2
stories.summary: President Trump threatened to strike Iran's power plants if Iran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 48 hours. Iran's military countered by threatening retaliatory attacks on US and regional allied energy infrastructure, IT systems, and water desalination facilities.

stories.title: Lebanon 22 March 2026 #1
stories.summary: On March 22, 2026, Israeli forces continued strikes in Iran, targeting military bases, arms production sites, and the intelligence ministry headquarters in Tehran. The IDF also struck Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon, killing three members including a Radwan Force commander.

stories.title: Israel 22 March 2026 #2
stories.summary: On March 22, Israeli forces struck military bases, arms production facilities, and the intelligence ministry headquarters in Tehran, Iran. The IDF simultaneously targeted Hezbollah positions in southern Lebanon, killing three Hezbollah members including a Radwan Force commander.

stories.title: Israel 23 March 2026 #1
stories.summary: On March 23, 2026, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu said President Trump saw an opportunity to leverage US-Israeli military achievements to end the war through a negotiated agreement. Netanyahu added that strikes continued in both Iran and Lebanon, targeting Iran's missile and nuclear programs and Hezbollah.

stories.title: Trump claims ‘very strong’ Iran talks as Tehran denies contact
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump claimed Monday that Washington was engaged in "very strong" talks with a respected Iranian leader, asserting Tehran was eager for a deal. Iran's government denied any contact with the United States.

stories.title: ‘Are You All Cowards?’: Russian Universities Pressure Students to Fight in Ukraine
stories.summary: Russian universities are increasingly pressuring students to enlist and fight in Ukraine as military recruitment numbers decline and war casualties rise. The effort represents a broadening of Moscow's search for fresh sources of combat personnel.

stories.title: Trump postpones Iran strikes; says deal is possible
stories.summary: President Trump postponed planned U.S. strikes on Iran, saying a deal was still possible. The decision followed Iranian threats to attack Israeli power plants and facilities supplying U.S. bases across the Gulf region if Washington targeted Iran's power infrastructure.

stories.title: Hong Kong government employee denies ordering surveillance of UK dissidents
stories.summary: Hong Kong government employee Chung Biu "Bill" Yuen denied allegations that he organized a surveillance operation targeting UK-based dissidents in London.

stories.title: Space Force anticipates first Kronos C2 contracts in April
stories.summary: The US Space Force expects to award its first contracts for the Kronos command-and-control system in April. Meanwhile, the related ATLAS C2 upgrade has not yet reached full operational viability, according to a DOT&E report.

stories.title: Russian recruiter found him in a World of Tanks chat. Threatened his mother and got him to plant two bombs in Bucha
stories.summary: A Russian recruiter contacted a suspect through a World of Tanks online chat, threatened his mother, and coerced him into planting two bombs in Bucha, Ukraine. Two police officers were injured in the resulting attack.

stories.title: Defense minister: “Air defense is one of NATO’s biggest challenges”
stories.summary: A drone that crossed into Lithuania from Belarus on 23 March exploded near the village of Lavišas without being detected by Lithuanian military or border guards. Lithuania's defense minister described air defense as one of NATO's biggest challenges.

stories.title: Mullin takes DHS helm as 100,000 employees remain unpaid
stories.summary: Senator Markwayne Mullin has been confirmed to lead the Department of Homeland Security as approximately 100,000 DHS employees remain unpaid. Mullin, entering his first executive-branch role, has pledged staffing rebuilds and organizational reforms.

stories.title: Zelenskyy: Russia plans to deploy control stations for long-range drones in Belarus
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russia is planning to deploy control stations in Belarus for long-range drones, citing Ukrainian intelligence reports about the expansion of Russia's drone control network.

stories.title: Trump Claims U.S., Iran Engaged in ‘Very Strong Talks’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump claimed the United States and Iran are engaged in significant diplomatic talks. However, Tehran has publicly denied that any such dialogue is taking place.

stories.title: Oil falls and shares rebound after Trump says talks have been held to end war
stories.summary: Oil prices fell and global stock markets rebounded after President Trump stated that "very good and productive" talks had been held to end the ongoing war.

stories.title: Russia, Vietnam Advance Plans for First Nuclear Power Plant
stories.summary: Russia and Vietnam are advancing plans to build Vietnam's first nuclear power plant. Vietnam is seeking to bolster its fuel reserves amid energy supply disruptions caused by the Middle East war.

stories.title: Russia Allows Private Security Firms to Use Firearms to Counter Drone Attacks
stories.summary: Russia has authorized private security firms to use firearms to counter drone attacks. The measure reflects Moscow's growing concern over the vulnerability of key infrastructure and assets to unmanned aerial strikes.

stories.title: Floods kill dozens, devastate farmland in Kenya [Africanews Today]
stories.summary: Flash floods and torrential rains have killed at least 81 people across Kenya this month. In Kisumu County, entire villages have been submerged and approximately 1,200 hectares of farmland destroyed.

stories.title: A web of sensors: How the US spots missiles and drones from Iran
stories.summary: The U.S. military uses a network of sensors to detect missiles and drones launched from Iran toward American bases in the region. The system provides early warning to service members, enabling them to take protective measures in time.

stories.title: EU Expresses Concern About Claims That Hungarian FM Shared Info With Russia
stories.summary: The European Union expressed concern over reports that Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó shared information from EU meetings with Russia. The Washington Post reported that Szijjártó regularly called Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov during breaks in EU sessions to relay what was discussed.

stories.title: Moscow Court Bans Galitsky’s Venture Capital Fund as ‘Extremist’
stories.summary: A Moscow court banned the venture capital fund of businessman Sergei Galitsky, designating it as "extremist." Approximately $100 million in assets belonging to Galitsky and connected individuals were also seized by the Russian government.

stories.title: Space Force’s two new cyber squadrons to defend space launch operations
stories.summary: The US Space Force established two new cyber squadrons dedicated to defending space launch operations. Maj. Torius Davis stated that adversaries are constantly seeking ways to deny, disrupt, or destroy US launch capabilities.

stories.title: US and UK teaming up to destroy underwater drones
stories.summary: The United States and United Kingdom are partnering to counter the threat of underwater drones to ports and critical infrastructure. The joint effort reflects growing concern about unmanned undersea vehicle threats from adversaries.

stories.title: A committed pharmacist and a homesick blogger – the Iranian civilians killed in the war
stories.summary: Civilian casualties are rising as the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran continues. The article profiles individual Iranian civilians killed in the conflict, including a pharmacist and a blogger.

stories.title: Czech defense firms tighten security after suspected arson at drone plant supplying Ukraine
stories.summary: Three Czech defense companies tightened physical security after a suspected arson attack at LPP Holding, a drone manufacturer in Pardubice that supplies AI-guided and strike drones to Ukraine.

stories.title: Blaming Israel Lets Washington Off the Hook
stories.summary: Former official Joe Kent resigned and published a letter mixing factual claims with misleading assertions about the war. The article argues that blaming Israel deflects accountability from Washington's own decision-making in the conflict.

stories.title: Nigerians in Lagos grapple with rising pump prices
stories.summary: Residents in Lagos, Nigeria, are struggling with soaring fuel prices driven by Middle East conflict disrupting global oil supplies. The rising costs are increasing the broader cost of living in the city.

stories.title: The Iran War’s Impact on Gas Markets May Be Felt for Years
stories.summary: The ongoing war with Iran is disrupting global gas markets, with effects expected to persist for years. Even after hostilities end, restoring normal energy flows through the region will take considerable time.

stories.title: Israel committing war crimes in Lebanon, HRW says
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch warned that Israel's escalation of military operations in Lebanon could constitute war crimes. The organization cited atrocities committed during the intensified conflict.

stories.title: Can Saudi Arabia's Yanbu port handle the switch from Hormuz?
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has attempted to increase oil exports through its Yanbu port on the Red Sea as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz. However, Yanbu's capacity falls significantly short of normal Hormuz shipping volumes.

stories.title: KC-135 crash in Iraq spurs calls for communications upgrades
stories.summary: A KC-135 tanker crash in Iraq has prompted calls to upgrade communications systems across the Air Force's aging tanker fleet. Nearly half of the KC-135 fleet reportedly lacks real-time battlefield connectivity systems.

stories.title: Anonymous social media accounts are calling for the secession of an Estonian county on Russia’s border. Tallinn says it’s Moscow’s doing.
stories.summary: Estonian authorities identified a cluster of anonymous social media accounts promoting a so-called 'Narva People's Republic,' targeting the border city of Narva where 85 percent of residents are ethnic Russian. Tallinn attributes the campaign to Moscow-directed information operations.

stories.title: Trump claims ‘major points of agreement’ with Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump gave Iran five additional days to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, claiming 'productive' talks with Tehran on the nuclear issue. Trump said major points of agreement had been reached.

stories.title: Meduza’s readers in Russia on life without Internet
stories.summary: Meduza surveyed its readers in Russia about worsening mobile internet shutdowns and restrictions. Hundreds of responses from dozens of cities described significant disruptions to everyday life and basic tasks.

stories.title: Watch: Inside Palestinian homes attacked by settlers
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian homes in the occupied West Bank after a teenage settler was killed, reportedly struck by a Palestinian-driven vehicle.

stories.title: Finnish President: Trump’s actions are making it harder to defeat Russia
stories.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb criticized U.S. President Trump's decision to ease oil sanctions on Russia, calling it 'very damaging' for Ukraine. Stubb estimated the move would provide Moscow with an additional $150 million in daily revenue.

stories.title: Warm Weather in Kamchatka Triggers Rapid Snowmelt After Winter of Historic Storms
stories.summary: Warm weather on Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula is triggering rapid snowmelt after a winter of historic storms. Powerful blizzards buried Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky under several feet of snow in January, much of which was never fully cleared.

stories.title: Israeli minister calls for annexation of southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's finance minister called for the annexation of southern Lebanon up to the Litani River as Israeli strikes continued in the area. Northern routes have been cut off, forcing civilian evacuations.

stories.title: Army receives first autonomous-ready, optionally piloted Black Hawk
stories.summary: The US Army has received its first autonomous-ready, optionally piloted H-60Mx Black Hawk helicopter. The aircraft was developed over more than a decade and is derived from DARPA's ALIAS autonomy program.

stories.title: In maps: Attacks across the Middle East
stories.summary: The US-Israel war with Iran has involved continued strikes on Tehran and Gulf states. President Trump has postponed a threatened strike on Iranian power plants.

stories.title: UAE accused of covert arms routes to Sudan's RSF
stories.summary: A report alleges the United Arab Emirates used covert cargo flights through Africa to supply arms to Sudan's Rapid Support Forces. The RSF has been accused of war crimes and possible genocide in the ongoing Sudanese conflict.

stories.title: Eid joy muted for South African Muslims as US, Israel bomb Iran
stories.summary: South African Muslims observed a subdued Eid al-Fitr amid the US-Israeli military operations against Iran and Israel's ongoing campaign in Gaza. The celebrations marking the end of Ramadan were overshadowed by regional conflict.

stories.title: EU sidelines Hungary in closed-door meetings as diplomats cite suspected Kremlin back-channel
stories.summary: European diplomats have begun sidelining Hungary in closed-door EU meetings after a European security official told the Washington Post that Budapest has been feeding Russia real-time information from those sessions.

stories.title: The US Army is already ditching its most powerful laser weapon yet
stories.summary: The U.S. Army has decided not to transition its 300-kilowatt Indirect Fire Protection Capability-High Energy Laser system to a program of record. The weapon, the Army's most powerful laser to date, will not proceed to full production.

stories.title: Five killed in Oman after vehicles swept away by floodwaters
stories.summary: Five people were killed in Oman after their vehicles were swept away by floodwaters caused by heavy rains. Authorities conducted rescue operations and issued warnings of continued severe weather conditions.

stories.title: Trump admin’s comments could undermine case against Anthropic in court: Experts
stories.summary: Legal experts say public comments by Trump administration officials could weaken the government's legal case against AI company Anthropic. Attorney Sean Timmons noted that the president's social media posts constitute "admissions against interest" that strengthen Anthropic's defense.

stories.title: Trump-linked firm secures deal to lobby for Libya's Haftar
stories.summary: Ballard Partners, a lobbying firm with ties to US President Donald Trump, signed a $2 million deal to represent Libyan commander Khalifa Haftar in Washington. Haftar faces long-standing allegations of human rights abuses.

stories.title: Ex-teacher accused of Scotland school abuse found guilty of sex attack in South Africa
stories.summary: A court in Cape Town, South Africa, found former teacher Iain Wares guilty of indecently assaulting a former student. The charges relate to sexual abuse allegations dating back to the 1980s at a school in Scotland.

stories.title: Could Iranian missiles reach London and Paris?
stories.summary: Experts have assessed whether Iranian missiles could reach London and Paris. While some analysts say Iran may have the range, such missiles would likely be intercepted before reaching their targets, and the overall risk is considered low.

stories.title: Foreign tourists fined, two drones seized after unauthorized flights over Norway’s main northern naval base
stories.summary: Norwegian police fined six foreign nationals and seized two drones after the individuals conducted unauthorized flights over Ramsund naval station, the Norwegian Navy's main base and logistics center in northern Norway. Three of the six are under further investigation.

stories.title: Briton held in Iran urges Starmer to reject spying claims
stories.summary: A British citizen detained in Iran has urged UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer to reject Iranian claims of espionage. The detainee and his partner have expressed fear for their lives amid the ongoing war and criticized the British government's response.

stories.title: Africa: Afreximbank and Fci to Host Africa Regional Conference On Factoring, Receivables Finance &amp; Credit Insurance in Kampala
stories.summary: The African Export-Import Bank and FCI announced they will co-host a conference on factoring, receivables finance, and credit insurance in Kampala, Uganda, on 15–16 April 2026, aimed at bridging Africa's trade finance gap.

stories.title: Why Lebanon's olive branch to Israel is misguided and dangerous
stories.summary: As France pushes for negotiations between Lebanon and Israel, analyst Imad K. Harb argues that Israel's military campaign in Lebanon points toward further territorial expansion rather than a peaceful resolution.

stories.title: Dangote refinery says begun fuel exports in Africa
stories.summary: Nigeria's Dangote mega-refinery has begun exporting fuel to other African countries. The move comes as global oil prices have risen sharply due to the ongoing war in the Middle East.

stories.title: Putin Urges Oil and Gas Companies to Use Iran War Windfall to Pay Off Bank Loans
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin urged Russian oil and gas companies to use windfall revenues from the Iran war to pay off bank loans. The Financial Times estimated the oil price surge is generating up to $150 million in additional daily revenue for Russia's state budget.

stories.title: Russia Sees Sharp Drop in Foreigners Taking Citizenship Amid Migration Crackdown
stories.summary: Russia saw a sharp decline in the number of foreigners obtaining citizenship amid a broader migration crackdown. Only 152,400 people received Russian passports last year, compared to 735,000 in 2021, the last full pre-war year.

stories.title: Lockheed Martin Australia, Rheinmetall exploring HIMARS sustainment Down Under
stories.summary: Lockheed Martin Australia and Rheinmetall are exploring a partnership to sustain HIMARS rocket launcher systems in Australia. If finalized, maintenance work on Lockheed's HIMARS would be conducted at a Rheinmetall facility in Queensland.

stories.title: Iran says it is implementing sentences against convicted January protesters
stories.summary: Iran announced it is enforcing sentences against individuals convicted in connection with January protests. The crackdown includes executions and has drawn international concern over human rights violations.

stories.title: Demand surges in Nigeria for new HIV prevention injection ahead of rollout
stories.summary: Demand is growing across Nigeria for a new long-acting HIV prevention injection, even ahead of its full nationwide rollout. The injectable option is generating significant public interest as an alternative to daily medication.

stories.title: Historic NATO visit: Admiral Pierre Vandier meets Ukrainian Chief of General Staff Andrii Hnatov in Kyiv
stories.summary: NATO Supreme Allied Commander Transformation Admiral Pierre Vandier visited Kyiv and met with Ukrainian Chief of General Staff Andrii Hnatov. Discussions focused on air defense and countering Russia's ongoing offensive.

stories.title: Watch: NATO chief: 22-nation group forming to secure Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: NATO's secretary general announced that a coalition of 22 nations was forming to secure the Strait of Hormuz amid rising tensions with Iran.

stories.title: Israel 'tortures Gaza toddler' to force 'confession' from father
stories.summary: Reports allege that Israeli soldiers tortured a Palestinian toddler in Gaza—burning the child with cigarettes and poking with metal nails—to coerce a confession from the child's father during interrogation.

stories.title: Saudi Aramco cuts oil supply to Asia for second month in April
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco reduced oil supply allocations to Asian customers for a second consecutive month in April. The company could not be immediately reached for comment.

stories.title: For Muslims and Iranians in US, a bittersweet Eid and Nowruz
stories.summary: Iranian Americans and Muslim communities across the United States marked a subdued Eid al-Fitr and Nowruz. The overlapping holidays were overshadowed by the ongoing conflict involving Iran, Israel, and the US.

stories.title: Nigerian heritage key to my success - Itauma
stories.summary: Heavyweight boxing prospect Moses Itauma discussed how a trip to his father's village in Nigeria helped him connect with his heritage. He credited his Nigerian roots as key to his success in the sport.

stories.title: US' and Iran's options for ending war narrow the longer it goes on
stories.summary: The US-Iran war faces a strategic stalemate, with Iran showing no willingness to back down and US air power alone proving insufficient to achieve Washington's primary objectives.

stories.title: Blast that injured two was 'terrorist attack', Ukrainian authorities say
stories.summary: Ukrainian authorities identified a blast that injured two people as a terrorist attack. The suspect, a 21-year-old local resident, claims he was blackmailed and coerced into planting the explosives.

stories.title: Nigerian police arrest 15 after viral videos of alleged sexual assault at festival
stories.summary: Nigerian police arrested 15 people after viral videos showing alleged sexual assaults at a festival provoked widespread outrage. The incident prompted the hashtag #StopRapingWomen to trend nationally on social media.

stories.title: London Jewish community ambulances set ablaze in suspected hate crime, police say
stories.summary: Ambulances belonging to London's Jewish community were set ablaze in what police are treating as an antisemitic hate crime.

stories.title: Only Diplomacy Can Resolve Middle East War, Kremlin Says
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said only diplomacy can resolve the Middle East war, stating that negotiations between Iran and the United States should have begun "yesterday."

stories.title: Iran Is Becoming America’s Ukraine
stories.summary: The U.S. war with Iran is shifting toward an attritional conflict focused on degrading energy infrastructure. Analysts warn this approach risks becoming a prolonged quagmire, drawing comparisons to the protracted conflict in Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran’s Biggest Wartime Advantage Is Geography
stories.summary: Iran's rugged terrain and extensive coastline are providing significant wartime advantages against U.S. and Israeli forces. The country's geography is shaping the course and character of the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Patriot missile involved in Bahrain blast likely US-operated, analysis finds
stories.summary: Analysis indicates that a Patriot missile involved in a pre-dawn explosion in Bahrain was likely U.S.-operated. The blast, occurring 10 days into the Iran war, injured dozens of civilians including children and damaged nearby homes.

stories.title: Dutch armed forces to add drone operators to combat brigades
stories.summary: The Dutch armed forces will add 1,000 to 1,200 personnel dedicated to drone and counter-drone operations within their combat brigades. The expansion represents a significant increase in the Netherlands' unmanned aerial systems capability.

stories.title: Guinea cracks down on suspected GSIM networks
stories.summary: Guinean authorities have dismantled a suspected terrorist network linked to the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (GSIM). Multiple foreign and Guinean nationals were arrested during a nationwide anti-terror operation.

stories.title: Ukraine Strikes Primorsk Port in Northwestern Russia, Damaging Fuel Reservoirs
stories.summary: Ukraine struck the Primorsk port in northwestern Russia, damaging fuel reservoirs. Industry sources told Reuters that Primorsk, one of Russia's largest oil export hubs, suspended operations on Monday following the attack.

stories.title: 'Do not doubt we will do this': Iran warns US against carrying out threat to strike power plants
stories.summary: Iran warned Monday it would strike electrical plants across the Middle East if the United States follows through on threats to bomb Iranian power stations. Tehran told Washington not to doubt its willingness to retaliate.

stories.title: World experiences hottest 11 years on record, WMO warns
stories.summary: The World Meteorological Organization has reported that the world just experienced its hottest 11-year period on record. The findings underscore the accelerating pace of global warming.

stories.title: Tencent integrates WeChat with OpenClaw AI agent amid China tech battle
stories.summary: Chinese tech giant Tencent integrated its WeChat messaging platform with an AI agent called ClawBot, powered by its OpenClaw technology. The bot appears as a contact within WeChat, giving over one billion monthly active users direct access to AI capabilities amid intensifying competition in China's tech sector.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia and the UAE targeted in fresh attacks
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates were targeted in fresh attacks. In Abu Dhabi, an Indian national was wounded by falling debris from an intercepted ballistic missile.

stories.title: Watch: Why is the assassination of Congo’s first PM Patrice Lumumba being talked about now?
stories.summary: Belgian diplomat Étienne Davignon, 93, is set to stand trial in connection with the 1961 assassination of Congolese Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba. Lumumba was shot, and his body was dismembered and dissolved in acid, with no one previously held accountable over more than six decades.

stories.title: Niger civil groups condemn EU call to free ex-president Bazoum
stories.summary: Civil society organizations in Niger condemned a European Union resolution demanding the release of former President Mohamed Bazoum. They called for simultaneous protests in Niger, Burkina Faso, and Mali against the EU's stance.

stories.title: As Gor makes first trip as U.S. Special envoy to South Asia, Delhi watches strategic signals closely
stories.summary: U.S. Special Envoy to South Asia Sergio Gor made his first trip in the role, visiting Colombo and the Maldives. India is closely monitoring the visit for strategic signals, with attention focused on possible future trips to Pakistan and Afghanistan.

stories.title: Lula slams ‘colonial mindset’ and UN failures at summit in Colombia
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva accused major powers of reviving a colonial approach toward developing nations at a summit in Colombia. He also criticized the United Nations for failing to address sovereignty concerns.

stories.title: US-made naval drone with active warhead washes up in northern Turkey, gets blown up
stories.summary: A U.S.-made AEGIR-W naval drone with an active warhead washed ashore on a beach in the Ünye district of Ordu province in northern Turkey. Turkish authorities subsequently detonated the vessel on site.

stories.title: Damaged Russian tanker adrift in Mediterranean to be towed to Libyan port
stories.summary: A damaged Russian gas tanker abandoned in the Mediterranean Sea will be towed to a Libyan port, according to a Libyan state-owned oil company. The vessel's condition and the circumstances of its abandonment remain under scrutiny.

stories.title: Australia's ABC staff to go on strike for first time in 20 years
stories.summary: Staff at Australia's ABC public broadcaster announced a 24-hour strike, the first in 20 years, expected to disrupt live television and radio broadcasts.

stories.title: Flash floods in Kenya have killed at least 81 and displace thousands
stories.summary: Torrential rains and flash floods have killed at least 81 people across Kenya, with Kisumu County among the hardest-hit areas. Approximately 1,200 hectares of farmland have been destroyed and thousands displaced.

stories.title: The Battlefield is the Next Betting Market
stories.summary: The article examines how prediction markets and open-source intelligence are increasingly forecasting military operations in real time. It contrasts the secrecy surrounding the U.S.-Israeli strike on Iran's nuclear facilities with the widely anticipated launch of Operation Epic Fury on February 28.

stories.title: Trump’s Visit to China Won’t Fix Much, If It Even Happens
stories.summary: President Trump suggested delaying his planned state visit to Beijing by about a month to focus on the war with Iran. He also called on China to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz, highlighting the fragility of the U.S.-China truce that had held since October.

stories.title: UK Defense confirms autonomous mine-hunting systems in war theatre; RN nuke powered sub in Arabian Sea
stories.summary: UK Defence Secretary John Healey confirmed that autonomous mine-hunting systems have been deployed to the Middle East during a visit to the Permanent Joint Armed Forces Headquarters at Northwood. Reports indicate the nuclear-powered submarine HMS Anson is positioned in the northern Arabian Sea within range of Iranian targets.

stories.title: Jihadist prisoner release secures fuel convoy truce in Mali
stories.summary: Mali released more than 100 suspected jihadist prisoners as part of a deal to end attacks on fuel convoys that had paralyzed the capital, Bamako. The agreement was confirmed by official and security sources.

stories.title: Can Middle Powers Gel?
stories.summary: The article examines whether middle powers can form an effective coalition in the current geopolitical environment. A detailed analysis reveals multiple barriers—including divergent interests and limited institutional frameworks—that hinder such cooperation.

stories.title: Electrostates vs. Petrostates
stories.summary: China is building a bloc of nations centered on green energy and electrification, while the United States is reinforcing its commitment to oil. The article contrasts these diverging energy strategies and their geopolitical implications.

stories.title: George H.W. Bush Won His Middle East War and Still Lost At Home
stories.summary: The article draws parallels between the current conflict and President George H.W. Bush's experience after the 1991 Gulf War. Despite military victory in the Middle East, Bush lost reelection when voters perceived him as more focused on foreign affairs than the domestic economy.

stories.title: Germany has a shortage of workers - so it's turning to India for help
stories.summary: Germany is recruiting skilled workers from India to address a significant domestic labor shortage. The program offers employment opportunities to young Indian professionals in the European nation.

stories.title: France's Socialists hold on to power in major cities in election boost for mainstream
stories.summary: France's Socialist Party retained control of Paris and Marseille in local elections, boosting mainstream political forces. The nationalist right won in Nice and several smaller towns.

stories.title: Israeli settlers target Palestinian villages in occupied West Bank, attacking people and properties
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank following the killing of 18-year-old settler Yehuda Sherman, who was reportedly struck by a Palestinian-driven vehicle while on a quad bike.

stories.title: National blackout hits Cuba for second time in a week
stories.summary: Cuba experienced its second national blackout in a week due to a total failure of its power grid. The crisis underscores the country's ongoing hardship exacerbated by a U.S.-imposed fuel blockade.

stories.title: Why did US and Israel attack Iran and how long could the war last?
stories.summary: The US and Israel launched strikes on Iran on 28 February, sparking a wider conflict that has spread across the Middle East.

stories.title: Israel to expand ground and air attacks against Hezbollah in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel is planning to expand ground and air operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon, raising fears among Lebanese residents of a large-scale ground invasion.

stories.title: Iranian missiles injure 180 in towns near Israeli nuclear site
stories.summary: Iranian ballistic missiles struck towns near an Israeli nuclear site, injuring 180 people. Israeli authorities are investigating how the missiles penetrated the country's advanced air defense systems.

stories.title: Abuja Alternate Festival returns with creative rejuvenation
stories.summary: The Abuja Alternate Festival returned to Nigeria's capital in 2026, marking a cultural revival for the city. The event brought together creative communities for artistic programming and rejuvenation.

stories.title: Russia Resumes Use of Space Launch Site Damaged in Accident
stories.summary: Russia launched a rocket from a Baikonur Cosmodrome site for the first time since the facility was damaged during a previous lift-off accident. The launch marks the resumption of operations at the affected site.

stories.title: DRC's Tshisekedi tasks PM with plan to save struggling national airline
stories.summary: DRC President Félix Tshisekedi has directed the prime minister to develop a new strategic plan for reviving the struggling national airline, Congo Airways. The carrier has faced persistent operational and financial difficulties.

stories.title: 'A direct hit' - BBC visits Israeli town after Iranian strike
stories.summary: The BBC reported from Dimona in southern Israel, where an Iranian missile scored a direct hit, highlighting the impact of Iranian strikes on Israeli civilian areas.

stories.title: Vietnam, Russia to Sign Energy Deal as PM Leaves for Moscow
stories.summary: Vietnam's prime minister departed for an official visit to Moscow, where the two countries plan to sign several agreements including an energy deal. The visit underscores deepening Russia-Vietnam cooperation.

stories.title: Russia Claims Control of Border Village in Ukraine's Sumy Region
stories.summary: Russia claimed control of a border village in Ukraine's Sumy region. The Russian army has been attempting to establish a buffer zone in the area for months, making incremental advances across the border.

stories.title: Qatari and Turkish citizens die in military helicopter crash
stories.summary: A military helicopter crash killed seven people, including four Qatari military personnel, one Turkish serviceman, and two technicians from a Turkish defense company.

stories.title: At least 13 children killed in strike on Sudanese hospital, WHO confirms
stories.summary: A strike on a hospital in western Darfur, Sudan, killed at least 64 people, including 13 children, according to the World Health Organization.

stories.title: US and Iran trade threats over Strait of Hormuz standoff
stories.summary: President Donald Trump threatened to destroy Iranian power plants unless Iran fully reopens the Strait of Hormuz within 48 hours. Iranian missiles struck two cities near Israel's primary nuclear research center.

stories.title: 'It's been bittersweet': The Iranian-Iraqi cafe drawing crowds to Hackney
stories.summary: Logma, a newly opened Iranian-Iraqi cafe in Hackney, London, has gone viral on social media for its sandwiches, drawing large crowds to the neighborhood.

stories.title: US troops in Nigeria using drones to detect and disrupt terrorist activity
stories.summary: U.S. military trainers deployed in Nigeria are conducting surveillance and intelligence-gathering operations using high-powered drones, according to the Nigerian military.

stories.title: How a medieval English abbey became a Chinese wedding destination
stories.summary: A medieval English abbey has become a popular wedding destination for Chinese couples, inspired by Taiwanese pop star Jay Chou's 2015 wedding held at the venue.

stories.title: Damaged Russian Tanker to Be Towed to Libya, State-Owned Company Says
stories.summary: Libya's National Oil Corporation announced it would collaborate with Italian energy group Eni to tow a damaged Russian tanker to Libya. The state-owned company confirmed the plan on Saturday.

stories.title: U.S., Ukrainian Teams Meet in Bid to Revive Talks on Ukraine War
stories.summary: U.S. and Ukrainian teams met in an effort to revive negotiations on the Ukraine war. Russian and Ukrainian negotiators have not met directly since last February in Geneva.

stories.title: Presidents of Kenya and Uganda launch next phase of cross-border railway
stories.summary: The presidents of Kenya and Uganda launched a new phase of the Standard Gauge Railway project aimed at linking East Africa to the Democratic Republic of Congo, advancing regional integration.

stories.title: 'Peace is a gradual thing': How land, cattle and identity fuel a deadly Nigerian conflict
stories.summary: Deadly violence persists in Nigeria's Plateau state, driven by disputes over land, cattle, and identity. Observers say a lack of justice and distrust of security forces continue to perpetuate the conflict between communities.

stories.title: Trump at a crossroads as US weighs tough options in Iran
stories.summary: President Trump has claimed the US-Iran war is nearly over, but conditions on the ground contradict those statements as the administration weighs difficult strategic options.

stories.title: Strike on Sudan hospital kills at least 64 and wounds 89 more, WHO reports
stories.summary: A drone strike on a healthcare facility in East Darfur, Sudan, killed at least 64 people and wounded 89 others, according to the World Health Organization. The victims included children and medical personnel, and the attack was attributed to the Sudanese army.

stories.title: Rwanda batter becomes youngest women's T20 centurion
stories.summary: Rwanda's Fanny Utagushimaninde became the youngest woman to score a century in T20 international cricket at 15 years and 223 days old. She described the achievement as a dream.

stories.title: Why there's no sign of the conflict in the Middle East 'winding down'
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister disputed President Trump's suggestion that the US was considering "winding down" the war, stating that Washington shows no readiness to halt its military aggression.

stories.title: Russia Condemns Reported Strikes on Iran Nuclear Site
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry condemned reported strikes on an Iranian nuclear site. Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova called the attacks "irresponsible" and warned they risked a "catastrophe" across the Middle East.

stories.title: Pavel Talankin Was a ‘Nobody Against Putin.’ Now He Has an Oscar.
stories.summary: Pavel Talankin's documentary "Mr. Nobody Against Putin" won the Oscar for Best Documentary Feature at the Academy Awards. Speaking afterward, Talankin said he believes the debate around the film is already changing Russian society.

stories.title: Germany pulls embassy staff out of Niger citing concerns over growing jihadist violence
stories.summary: Germany temporarily withdrew its diplomatic staff from Niger due to escalating security concerns linked to jihadist violence in the West African nation.

stories.title: Chad to deploy 800 troops to Haiti's Gang Suppression Force as Kenya steps back
stories.summary: Chad is preparing to deploy approximately 800 police officers to Haiti to join an international force combating widespread gang activity, as Kenya scales back its involvement.

stories.title: Putin Sends Nowruz Wishes to Iran Amid Ongoing War
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin sent Nowruz holiday wishes to Iran amid the ongoing war there. Russia, a longtime Iranian ally, has condemned the U.S.-Israeli strikes on the country that began on February 28.

stories.title: Ukraine Launches More Than 280 Drones at Russia in One of Its Largest Strikes
stories.summary: Ukraine launched more than 280 drones at Russia in one of its largest aerial strikes since the war began. No further details on specific targets or damage were immediately provided.

stories.title: US lifts sanctions on some Iranian oil as energy prices soar
stories.summary: The US Treasury lifted sanctions on certain Iranian oil exports amid soaring energy prices. Treasury Secretary said the move would bring approximately 140 million barrels of oil to global markets.

stories.title: A new threat to global shipping as Yemen's Houthis threaten to close vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi forces threatened to block the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to ships from countries they consider aggressors against members of the "axis of resistance," posing a new risk to global shipping.

stories.title: UK allows US to use bases to strike Strait of Hormuz targets
stories.summary: The UK government authorized the US to use British military bases for strikes on targets in the Strait of Hormuz. Downing Street said ministers approved the expansion after accusing Iran of "reckless strikes."

stories.title: ‘This is the saddest moment’: families search for loved ones on Eid after Kabul hospital strike
stories.summary: Pakistan conducted airstrikes on what it said was terrorist and military infrastructure in Afghanistan, but a drug rehabilitation centre in Kabul was reportedly hit, killing at least 400 people according to the Taliban. Families spent the Eid holiday searching for loved ones in unmarked mass graves.

stories.title: BTS Arirang review: K-pop idols rekindle their fire
stories.summary: BTS released their tenth album, "Arirang," which marks a return to the rebellious, rap-heavy sound that characterized their early career.

stories.title: Russia's school propaganda was  highlighted by Oscar-winning film - but does it work?
stories.summary: An Oscar-winning film highlighted Russia's use of school propaganda to promote support for its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The messaging frames the war as defensive and equates patriotism with unquestioning loyalty.

stories.title: The forgotten Indian woman trailblazer in British medicine
stories.summary: In 1912, Jamini Sen became the first woman Fellow of Glasgow's Royal College, a medical institution founded in 1599 that had long excluded women from fellowship.

stories.title: US countered drone threat over ‘strategic’ installation in early hours of Operation Epic Fury: Guillot
stories.summary: U.S. Northern Command used a Fly-Away Kit to counter a drone threat over a "strategic" U.S. installation during the early hours of Operation Epic Fury, according to commander General Gregory Guillot. The incident highlights emerging drone threats to domestic military facilities.

stories.title: Iranian strikes on bases used by US caused $800m in damage, new analysis shows
stories.summary: New analysis reveals that Iranian retaliatory strikes on bases used by US forces caused approximately $800 million in damage, with most destruction occurring in the first week after the US-Israeli operation began.

stories.title: Attacked Russian Tanker Drifting Toward Libya – Italian Authorities
stories.summary: A damaged Russian tanker is drifting toward Libya, according to Italian authorities. Officials described the vessel as severely damaged, noting that towing it would be a complex operation despite the ship remaining afloat.

stories.title: Russia Offered to End Iran Intelligence Sharing if U.S. Halted Ukraine Support – Politico
stories.summary: Politico reported that Russia offered to end intelligence sharing with Iran if the United States halted its support for Ukraine. Russia has expanded intelligence-sharing and military cooperation with Tehran since the U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran on February 28.

stories.title: Ukraine-Hungary oil pipeline row threatens EU loan
stories.summary: Ukraine and Hungary are in a dispute over the condition of an oil transit hub in western Ukraine that was damaged by a Russian strike. The disagreement over the extent of damage threatens an EU loan, as oil flow through the pipeline remains suspended.

stories.title: UK approves US use of British bases to strike Iran missile sites targeting ships
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer approved the use of British bases for U.S. strikes on Iranian missile sites that were targeting ships. Starmer had initially rejected the U.S. request, requiring assurance that any military action would be legally justified.

stories.title: Krasnodar Brings Back Analog Air Raid Sirens Amid Worsening Internet Disruptions
stories.summary: The Russian city of Krasnodar has reinstated analog air raid sirens due to worsening internet disruptions. Krasnodar is among dozens of Russian regions experiencing increasingly frequent and prolonged internet outages in recent weeks.

stories.title: The Kremlin appears to be blocking Telegram. Meduza asked its Russia-based readers how well the crackdown is working.
stories.summary: Russian authorities appear to have begun blocking or severely restricting the messaging app Telegram, with availability dropping to 75 percent and nearly 80 percent of requests to Telegram domains failing, according to monitoring groups and the outlet Kommersant.

stories.title: Two suspected Iranian spies reportedly arrested near UK submarine base
stories.summary: Two suspected Iranian spies were reportedly arrested near the UK's nuclear submarine base at Faslane, Scotland, according to the Sun newspaper. The arrests come amid heightened tensions between Iran and Western nations during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Zelensky Says Ukraine Targeting Kremlin-Backed Messaging App Max
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is targeting the Kremlin-backed messaging app Max. He noted it was becoming "difficult to transmit signals" to Russians amid mounting restrictions on the Telegram platform.

stories.title: Ukraine deploys units to 5 Middle East countries to intercept drones
stories.summary: Ukraine has deployed units to five Middle Eastern countries to help intercept drones during the Iran conflict. President Zelenskyy said Kyiv seeks financial and technological compensation in return, noting the U.S. was among nations requesting Ukrainian assistance.

stories.title: Navy bets $900M on automated factories to boost submarine production
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy awarded a $900 million contract to four-year-old company Hadrian for automated manufacturing to boost submarine production. The investment aims to offset worker shortages in the submarine industrial base.

stories.title: Defense workers' morale has plunged under Trump, survey finds
stories.summary: A survey finds that morale among defense civilian workers has dropped significantly under the Trump administration. Only 9 percent of Army civilians reported finding Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's leadership motivating.

stories.title: France Seizes False-Flagged Oil Tanker Coming From Russia
stories.summary: France seized a false-flagged oil tanker arriving from Russia. President Emmanuel Macron said France "will not allow" shadow fleet ships to profit while helping finance Russia's war effort.

stories.title: ‘Deeply Concerning’: Russia Could Face Diabetes ‘Epidemic,’ Social Policy Chief Warns
stories.summary: A senior Russian social policy official warned that Russia could face a diabetes "epidemic." Health Ministry estimates indicate more than 6 million adults and 65,000 children in Russia live with diabetes, a figure that has more than doubled over the past 20 years.

stories.title: A longtime pro-Putin blogger published a tirade against the Russian president. Now he’s in a psychiatric hospital.
stories.summary: Pro-Kremlin blogger Ilya Remeslo published a Telegram post titled 'Five reasons why I stopped supporting Vladimir Putin.' Days later, he was reportedly hospitalized at a psychiatric facility in St. Petersburg.

stories.title: On the Radar: Latin America Keeps Attacking Crime — But Is It Working?
stories.summary: Ecuador conducted bombings along its border with Colombia, while one of the region's most wanted traffickers was arrested. Chile announced additional hardline anti-crime measures, as analysts question the effectiveness of Latin America's escalating security crackdowns.

stories.title: Texelis, Scata team up on medium-heavy vehicle that can do drone defense
stories.summary: French firms Texelis and Scata have partnered to develop the MK1, an 18-ton medium-heavy vehicle capable of drone defense. The multirole platform was developed in under a year and incorporates lessons learned from the Ukraine war.

stories.title: Conflict and Consequences
stories.summary: Israel announced and Tehran confirmed the killing of Ali Larijani, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, on March 17. His death follows the earlier elimination of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei at the start of the U.S.-Israeli offensive, removing the regime's top coordinator.

stories.title: Russian Central Bank Lowers Key Rate to 15%
stories.summary: Russia's central bank lowered its key interest rate to 15%. Policymakers cited an increasingly uncertain economic and inflationary outlook stemming from the Iran war.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Strike Kills Man in Belgorod Region
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike killed a man in Russia's Belgorod region. The victim died in the village of Murom, located across the border from eastern Ukraine's Kharkiv region.

stories.title: This missile just proved itself in Iran. The US needs more, ASAP
stories.summary: The Precision Strike Missile has demonstrated its effectiveness in combat operations during the Iran conflict. Despite its proven capabilities, analysts note the weapon has been procured in relatively small quantities and call for accelerated production.

stories.title: Lukoil Reports $12Bln Loss in 2025 as Sanctions Force Foreign Asset Write-Off
stories.summary: Russian oil giant Lukoil reported a $12 billion loss in 2025 after sanctions forced a write-off of foreign assets. The company wrote off investments in its international business unit, Lukoil International, at an estimated cost of $20.2 billion.

stories.title: Venezuelan leader replaces senior military commanders
stories.summary: Venezuelan leader Delcy Rodríguez replaced senior military commanders, including appointing a new defence minister. Human rights groups described the reshuffle as a "recycling of impunity."

stories.title: U.S. Tightens Sanctions Waiver on Russian Oil After Tanker Reportedly Delivers Fuel to Cuba
stories.summary: The U.S. tightened its sanctions waiver on Russian oil after reports that a Russian tanker delivered fuel to Cuba. The Treasury Department's amendment on Thursday followed Cuba's deepening energy crisis, which has caused widespread blackouts.

stories.title: Oil prices, fear of Trump? China mysteriously reduced warplane activity near Taiwan
stories.summary: Analysts report a mysterious decrease in Chinese warplane sorties near Taiwan in recent weeks. Possible explanations include rising oil prices due to the Iran conflict and concerns about provoking the Trump administration.

stories.title: Weather tracker: Unseasonal storms hit parts of Pakistan and India
stories.summary: Severe unseasonal storms struck southern Pakistan and northwest India, with Karachi recording over 50mm of rain and wind gusts up to 60 mph. At least 18 people were killed in Karachi as walls, buildings, and a pedestrian bridge collapsed amid flooding and widespread power outages.

stories.title: Madagascar’s military ruler decrees that ministers must pass lie detector tests
stories.summary: Madagascar's military president Michael Randrianirina has decreed that new ministers must pass lie detector tests, claiming the measure will root out corruption. Randrianirina seized power in an October coup following youth-led protests but quickly drew criticism for appointing officials seen as part of the old elite.

stories.title: Japan’s new ‘ugly duckling’ electronic-warfare aircraft takes to the sky
stories.summary: Japan's new electronic-warfare aircraft has completed its first flight as the country ramps up spending on electronic-warfare capabilities. Questions remain about how many of the aircraft Japan will ultimately procure.

stories.title: Space, Cyber Significant Factors in Operation Epic Fury
stories.summary: Space and cyber capabilities played significant roles in Operation Epic Fury, with military planners integrating satellite-based assets and cyber operations as key components of the campaign's execution.

stories.title: Trump makes Pearl Harbor remark in meeting with Japan's PM
stories.summary: During a meeting with Japan's Prime Minister, President Trump compared U.S. strikes on Iran to the 1941 Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor.

stories.title: What It Was Like to Be Under Incoming Fire from the War on Terror to Today
stories.summary: A crossover podcast episode features military veterans discussing their experiences with indirect fire and bombardment across conflicts from the War on Terror to the present. The hosts provide context on the current Middle East threat environment and share advice for deployed troops.

stories.title: Why Did the United States Lift Sanctions on Assad’s Chemical Weapons Scientists?
stories.summary: On June 30, 2025, the Trump administration revised Syria sanctions as part of normalizing relations with Damascus after Bashar al-Assad's overthrow. In the process, 266 employees of Syria's Scientific Studies and Research Center—the hub of Assad's chemical weapons program—were quietly removed from the U.S. Treasury's sanctions list without explanation.

stories.title: What the Donroe Doctrine Could Mean for China’s Economic Statecraft
stories.summary: In early 2026, the Trump administration launched military interventions in Iran and Venezuela and threatened annexation of Greenland, prompting European leaders to engage more closely with Beijing. China is weighing its options under the new U.S. "Donroe Doctrine" ahead of a planned U.S.-China summit in late March.

stories.title: Colombia's budding tech scene needs a cash boost
stories.summary: Colombia has emerged as a technology hub for Latin America, attracting startups and tech companies. However, the country's budding tech scene faces challenges in securing sufficient investment.

stories.title: Desperate for food, drought-stricken Kenyans turn to the gingerbread tree
stories.summary: Some 26 million people across Kenya, Ethiopia, and Somalia face extreme hunger, according to Oxfam. Drought-stricken communities in Kenya are turning to the gingerbread tree as a food source amid the crisis.

stories.title: The case for the US Army to procure the KNDS RCH 155 howitzer
stories.summary: Advocates argue the U.S. Army should procure the KNDS RCH 155 howitzer to address a critical modernization gap in field artillery. The wheeled, automated artillery system is presented as a transformative solution for the service's future fire-support needs.

stories.title: High-speed combat drone production starts at new US Anduril plant in days
stories.summary: Anduril Industries will begin producing high-speed loyal wingman combat drones within days at a new manufacturing facility in Ohio. The plant is opening months ahead of schedule to meet growing demand for autonomous combat aircraft.

stories.title: What Does the Exit of Vladimir Padrino López Mean for Organized Crime in Venezuela?
stories.summary: The dismissal of Venezuelan former defence minister Vladimir Padrino López raises questions about future criminal dynamics in the country. Analysts are examining implications for the Cartel of the Suns, a network allegedly involving senior military officials in drug trafficking.

stories.title: Ros Atkins on... Trump's mixed messages on the war
stories.summary: BBC Analysis Editor Ros Atkins examined President Trump's contradictory public statements regarding the US war with Iran.

stories.title: Belarus Frees 250 Political Prisoners in U.S.-Brokered Deal
stories.summary: Belarus released 250 political prisoners as part of a deal brokered by the United States. In exchange, Washington agreed to remove sanctions on several Belarusian companies.

stories.title: Tanker 'Likely' Delivered Russian Diesel to Fuel-Starved Cuba
stories.summary: A tanker reportedly delivered Russian diesel fuel to Cuba, which would be the first arrival of a refined petroleum product to the island since January. Cuba has been grappling with a severe energy shortage.

stories.title: Internet Outages Costing Russian Lives, Belgorod Governor Warns
stories.summary: Belgorod Governor Vyacheslav Gladkov warned that internet outages in the region are costing Russian lives. He said he raised the issue of regular mobile internet disruptions in recent meetings with federal authorities in Moscow.

stories.title: Telegram news channels are one of Russia’s few major alternatives to state media. The head of one of the largest says their days may be numbered.
stories.summary: Russian authorities have apparently begun blocking Telegram, threatening independent news channels on the platform. The head of Ostorozhno, Novosti — one of Telegram's largest news channels, launched in 2021 as part of Ksenia Sobchak's media holding — warned that such outlets' days may be numbered.

stories.title: Ukraine’s counteroffensive brings gains in the south but weakens other sectors of the front. Meduza analyzes the latest battlefield developments.
stories.summary: Ukraine's counteroffensive has yielded territorial gains in southern Ukraine but has reportedly weakened other sectors of the front line. The analysis is based on open-source battlefield information.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine Exchanging Around 1K Bodies Each Month, Red Cross Chief Says
stories.summary: The International Committee of the Red Cross disclosed that Russia and Ukraine are exchanging approximately 1,000 bodies each month. ICRC Director-General Pierre Krahenbuhl noted the scale of consequences when military means are deployed between states.

stories.title: RT Crew Narrowly Escapes Israeli Strike in Lebanon During Live Broadcast
stories.summary: An RT news crew narrowly escaped an Israeli strike in Lebanon during a live broadcast. Russia's Foreign Ministry claimed the strike was "not accidental" and called for an international response to the incident.

stories.title: Indian film board blocks release of Oscar-nominated Gaza drama The Voice of Hind Rajab
stories.summary: India's Central Board of Film Certification blocked the release of the Oscar-nominated Tunisian docudrama The Voice of Hind Rajab, about the death of a five-year-old Palestinian girl during the Israel-Gaza war. The film's Indian distributor said authorities warned that screening the film could harm India-Israel relations.

stories.title: A-10s are striking Iranian boats. Some say it’s a ‘wake-up call’ to stop the Warthog’s retirement.
stories.summary: A-10 Warthog aircraft are conducting strikes against Iranian boats during Operation Epic Fury, renewing debate over the aircraft's planned retirement. Congress paused the A-10's retirement last year, and its combat role in the Iran conflict has strengthened arguments to keep the fleet operational.

stories.title: Watch: Missile lands next to presenter during live report from Lebanon
stories.summary: During a live broadcast from Lebanon, RT correspondent Steve Sweeney was forced to dive off-screen when a missile struck near his position.

stories.title: LDPR Kicks Out Clout-Chasing State Duma Lawmaker
stories.summary: Russia's LDPR party expelled State Duma lawmaker Andrei Svintsov. Svintsov had in recent months been the source of prominent headlines about proposed internet restrictions in Russia.

stories.title: Regions Calling: In Russia, All Eyes Are on Siberia’s Farmers
stories.summary: Small-scale farmers across Siberia are resisting government-mandated livestock culls, refusing to surrender thousands of animals despite official orders.

stories.title: Kremlin Slams ‘Irresponsible’ Ukrainian Drone Attacks on TurkStream and Blue Stream Compressor Stations
stories.summary: Gazprom reported that Russian military forces intercepted 26 Ukrainian drones targeting energy infrastructure in the Krasnodar region. The Kremlin condemned the attacks on the TurkStream and Blue Stream compressor stations as irresponsible.

stories.title: South Korea Joins East Asian Countries Weighing Russian Oil Purchases
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung indicated the country is considering purchasing Russian oil, stating that urgent efforts are needed to secure alternative crude supplies amid ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: ‘It takes money to kill bad guys,’ Hegseth says of $200B Iran war request to Congress
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has requested $200 billion from Congress to fund the ongoing war against Iran, stating "it takes money to kill bad guys." Hegseth also called on allied nations to show gratitude to President Trump for U.S. military efforts.

stories.title: US intelligence elevates AI as a top global threat in new report
stories.summary: The U.S. intelligence community's latest annual threat assessment elevates AI as a top global threat, citing its use in combat and economic competition. Notably, the report from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence omits AI-driven disinformation as a concern.

stories.title: Small Firms Signal New Phase in China’s Expanding Footprint in Brazil
stories.summary: Smaller Chinese companies are establishing a growing commercial presence in Brazil, marking a new phase in China's economic expansion in the country that extends beyond the large state-backed enterprises that previously dominated bilateral trade.

stories.title: Pequeñas empresas marcan nueva etapa en la expansión de China en Brasil
stories.summary: Pequeñas empresas chinas están estableciendo una creciente presencia comercial en Brasil, señalando una nueva fase en la expansión económica de China que va más allá de las grandes empresas estatales que anteriormente dominaban el comercio bilateral.

stories.title: Countering Drones and the Pace of Modern War
stories.summary: A podcast featuring leaders from AeroVironment, Epirus, and Hidden Level discusses counter-drone solutions and broader challenges in how the U.S. military adapts to modern warfare. The conversation addresses defense procurement problems and the pace of adaptation by both the United States and its adversaries.

stories.title: The Inevitability of Chinese Military Purges
stories.summary: Since 2022, Chinese leader Xi Jinping has purged more than 100 senior military officials, including the January 2026 removal of top general Zhang Youxia, vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission. Five of six Central Military Commission generals have been removed in less than three years.

stories.title: Islamic State Containment Is Collapsing in Syria
stories.summary: Following the repeal of Caesar Act sanctions, Syria's transitional president Ahmad al Sharaa launched an offensive against the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces, triggering territorial losses and Arab tribal defections. The resulting security breakdown has undermined Islamic State containment in northeast Syria, including mass escapes from al-Hol refugee camp.

stories.title: South Africans say criminal gangs are exploiting the water crisis
stories.summary: Residents in parts of South Africa report that criminal gangs are exploiting an ongoing water crisis. Some communities have been without mains water supply for weeks.

stories.title: Russian authorities are culling livestock over a mysterious disease. Farmers are protesting, saying their animals don’t look sick.
stories.summary: Farmers in Russia's Novosibirsk region have been protesting for nearly two weeks against the mass confiscation and culling of their livestock by authorities citing an unnamed 'especially dangerous disease.' Villagers dispute that their animals are sick and object to the low compensation offered.

stories.title: China en Latinoamérica: compromiso estratégico, influencia y riesgo democrático – PARTE II
stories.summary: An analysis examines China's strategic engagement in Latin America, focusing on its influence and potential risks to democratic governance in the region. This is the second part of a multi-part investigation.

stories.title: China na América Latina: Compromisso estratégico, influência e risco democrático – PARTE I
stories.summary: A Portuguese-language analysis explores China's strategic engagement across Latin America, examining Beijing's growing influence and the potential democratic risks it poses in the region. This is the first part of a multi-part series.

stories.title: China in Latin America: Strategic Engagement, Leverage, and Democratic Risk – PART I
stories.summary: An investigation examines China's expanding strategic engagement across Latin America, assessing Beijing's leverage and the democratic risks posed by its deepening economic and political ties in the region.

stories.title: Anduril: new factory will start making drone wingman in just ‘days’
stories.summary: Anduril Industries announced that its new Ohio manufacturing facility will begin producing loyal wingman combat drones within days, months ahead of the original schedule. The factory is intended to support scaled production of autonomous combat aircraft.

stories.title: Russia Sends Oil and Gas Tankers to Crisis-Hit Cuba, Defying U.S. Blockade – FT
stories.summary: Russia has dispatched oil and gas tankers to Cuba in defiance of the U.S. blockade, according to the Financial Times. If the ships arrive, they would represent Cuba's first energy shipments in three months.

stories.title: Defense Business Brief: DOD lab audits?; Notes from McAleese; Spotlight on Alabama manufacturing
stories.summary: The Department of Defense is considering audits of its laboratory system, alongside developments noted at the McAleese defense conference and a spotlight on Alabama's defense manufacturing sector.

stories.title: Syria and the Islamic State: Analyzing America’s Departure
stories.summary: The article revisits Thanassis Cambanis's 2024 argument that the United States should withdraw from Syria while continuing counter-terrorism efforts against the Islamic State. Two years later, following an American withdrawal and a new Syrian government, Cambanis reassesses his original recommendations.

stories.title: 5 Models of Criminal Control Over Fentanyl Markets in Northern Mexico
stories.summary: An investigation identifies five distinct models of criminal control over fentanyl markets in northern Mexico. Local drug markets in the region operate beyond simple supply-and-demand dynamics, with criminal organizations dictating pricing, distribution methods, and sales locations.

stories.title: How Fentanyl Was Introduced in Mexico’s Local Drug Markets
stories.summary: Mexican criminal organizations that became primary suppliers of illicit fentanyl to the United States have also fostered pockets of domestic fentanyl consumption. These local markets have emerged along key trafficking corridors in Mexico since at least several years ago.

stories.title: How Criminal Decisions Over the Drug Market Impact Public Health in Northern Mexico
stories.summary: Criminal actors' decisions about drug supply in northern Mexico's local markets are significantly impacting public health outcomes. The situation challenges international drug policy efforts increasingly oriented toward public health strategies.

stories.title: DNI's threat assessment omits foreign election interference
stories.summary: The Director of National Intelligence's annual threat assessment omits mention of foreign election interference. DNI Tulsi Gabbard's contradictory testimony on Iran's nuclear program has highlighted tensions between the intelligence community and the White House's justifications for the war.

stories.title: ‘Wake up already’: Internet disruptions and Telegram outages fuel growing anger among Russian users
stories.summary: Internet disruptions and Telegram outages across Russia are fueling growing anger among users. Monitoring data shows Telegram availability dropped significantly, with up to one in four messages failing to reach recipients.

stories.title: La profundidad del engaño: la sombra militar sobre la expedición “científica” china a Chile
stories.summary: An investigation examines alleged military dimensions behind a Chinese expedition described as scientific in Chile. The report suggests the operation carried a hidden military shadow beneath its stated research purposes.

stories.title: The Depth of Deception: The Military Shadow Over China’s ‘Scientific’ Chilean Expedition
stories.summary: An investigation alleges that a Chinese expedition to Chile presented as scientific had concealed military objectives. The report examines what it describes as deceptive practices surrounding the operation.

stories.title: Military Operational Thinking in an Age of Artificial Intelligence
stories.summary: The article examines how artificial intelligence is being integrated into military planning and operational design. It responds to concerns about a perceived decline in operational art, exploring whether AI tools are improving or complicating coherence and integration in military operations.

stories.title: Double-Edged Swords: How Military Purges Shape Authoritarian Appetite for War
stories.summary: In January 2026, China's defense ministry announced that top general Zhang Youxia was under investigation, making him the fifth of six Central Military Commission generals removed since 2022. The article analyzes how military purges in authoritarian regimes can either pave the way for war or undermine military effectiveness.

stories.title: Bailing Out Russia for “Peace” Is a Losing Proposition
stories.summary: In February 2026, Russia proposed a $14 trillion economic reintegration package—the "Dmitriev package"—seeking sanctions relief, access to dollar-based financial systems, and energy joint ventures with Western nations. Critics argue that accepting the proposal would underwrite the very system the West has spent four years trying to contain.

stories.title: Drinking from the Bitter Chalice in the Middle East, Again
stories.summary: The article draws a parallel between Iran's current situation and Ayatollah Khomeini's acceptance of a UN ceasefire in 1988 after eight years of war with Iraq. It examines how the Islamic Republic survived that defeat without moderating and rebuilt its proxy networks over subsequent decades.

stories.title: Telegram is full of channels posting videos of Ukrainian POWs being killed and their bodies desecrated. Many are run by teenagers.
stories.summary: An investigation by iStories found that Russian-language Telegram channels posting graphic footage of Ukrainian POW killings and corpse desecration are largely run by civilians, often teenagers, rather than soldiers.

stories.title: Agents of Chaos: Unpacking the Actions of Border Patrol Agents Across the US
stories.summary: A joint investigation by Bellingcat, Evident Media, and CalMatters examined the actions of US Border Patrol agents operating far from border areas. One case involved a gardener named Ernesto Campos who was stopped by Border Patrol agents in Bakersfield, California, well inland from the border.

stories.title: Watch: Sean Penn receives 'Oscar' in Ukraine after skipping US ceremony
stories.summary: American actor Sean Penn received his third Academy Award but did not attend the ceremony in the United States. Instead, he traveled to Ukraine, where the award was presented to him.

stories.title: Record-smashing $1.5-trillion spending proposal will fund only the ‘most essential things’: comptroller
stories.summary: The Pentagon's acting comptroller said the proposed record $1.5 trillion defense budget will fund only the "most essential things." Officials also noted that only a small portion of the $153 billion in reconciliation funds remains unallocated.

stories.title: Takeaways from China’s National People’s Congress Meeting
stories.summary: China held its annual National People's Congress and Political Consultative Conference from March 5 to 12, also presenting its 15th Five-Year Plan through 2030. Four experts analyze key takeaways regarding China's economic and political priorities.

stories.title: Russia was expected to block Telegram in April. It appears to have done it two weeks early.
stories.summary: Russian authorities appear to have blocked the messaging app Telegram approximately two weeks ahead of an anticipated early-April deadline. Users across multiple regions reported major outages over the weekend of March 14–15.

stories.title: Russia adds Meduza editor-in-chief Ivan Kolpakov to its wanted list
stories.summary: Meduza editor-in-chief Ivan Kolpakov has been added to the Russian Interior Ministry's wanted list, according to the outlet Mediazona.

stories.title: US counterterrorism chief resigns over Iran war
stories.summary: Joe Kent, the US counterterrorism chief, resigned over the US military campaign against Iran, stating that Iran posed no imminent threat to the United States. He alleged the attack was launched following pressure from Israel.

stories.title: How Does the Iran War Affect China’s Energy Security?
stories.summary: Despite importing over 10 percent of its oil from Iran, China is approximately 85 percent energy self-sufficient with diversified international sources and growing domestic electrification. Beijing has built a cushion against short-term supply shocks from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Open War at the Durand Line: Can Pakistan’s Escalation Compel a Taliban Recalculation?
stories.summary: In February 2026, Pakistan declared open war on Afghanistan, striking Taliban military installations in Kabul and Kandahar after months of failed indirect pressure. The escalation marked a shift from targeting non-state militants to directly attacking Taliban-governed Afghanistan's military assets.

stories.title: Young Venezuelans voice hope and frustration as post-Maduro future unfolds
stories.summary: Young Venezuelans are expressing both hope and frustration as the country navigates a post-Maduro political transition. U.S. forces seized former President Maduro, and young people who grew up under his rule are adjusting to a changing political landscape.

stories.title: US Navy to use wall-climbing robots to inspect ships
stories.summary: Gecko Robotics has secured a $71 million contract with the US Navy to deploy wall-climbing robots for ship inspections. The robots are intended to aid hull and structural assessments aboard naval vessels.

stories.title: 'Fire came from the sky and burned them' - life on the brink of civil war in South Sudan
stories.summary: The South Sudanese army has warned of a major military offensive in Jonglei state, prompting approximately 50,000 people to flee their homes. Residents describe devastating aerial attacks on civilian areas.

stories.title: The US built a blueprint to avoid civilian war casualties. Trump officials scrapped it
stories.summary: Trump administration officials reportedly dismantled a US government framework designed to minimize civilian casualties during military operations. The blueprint had been developed to guide wartime targeting decisions.

stories.title: Fifa sanctions Nigeria and DR Congo over World Cup play-off
stories.summary: FIFA has sanctioned both the Nigeria Football Federation and the DR Congo Football Association over disciplinary breaches by supporters during World Cup play-off matches. Both federations face fines.

stories.title: Wary allies show there's no quick fix to Trump's Iran crisis
stories.summary: European leaders are reluctant to assist the US in securing the Strait of Hormuz but recognize that inaction regarding the Iran war is untenable, highlighting the lack of a quick diplomatic resolution.

stories.title: Senior FSB official’s son linked to company supplying Russia’s Internet censorship systems, investigation finds
stories.summary: An investigation by journalist Andrey Zakharov found that the son of a senior FSB official holds a position and likely a financial stake in the holding company that supplies hardware used to restrict and surveil Russian internet traffic.

stories.title: Investing in Women is Investing in the Future
stories.summary: This installment of The Ukraine Compass, a weekly digest for War on the Rocks members, curates Ukrainian media commentary on issues shaping the country. The edition focuses on the role of investing in women as part of Ukraine's future during wartime.

stories.title: A Russian soccer player murdered a woman after phone scammers tricked him into robbing her — and tricked her daughter into letting him in.
stories.summary: A Moscow woman was killed by a man who was allegedly manipulated by phone scammers into believing he was conducting a police operation. The suspect, a Russian soccer player, carried out the attack after the scammers also tricked the victim's daughter into letting him into the home.

stories.title: Russia’s long-anticipated block of messenger app Telegram has begun, experts say
stories.summary: Experts say Russia's long-anticipated block of Telegram has begun, with the messaging app largely ceasing to function inside the country according to user reports on outage-tracking websites.

stories.title: The Danger of Vibe Patriotism in Defense Tech
stories.summary: The article critiques the growing trend among defense technology startups and venture capital firms of framing their commercial work as a form of national service comparable to military duty. Companies like Palantir and Anduril are cited as examples of this messaging phenomenon.

stories.title: Don’t Count Launches: Misreading Iran’s Drone Capacity
stories.summary: The article warns against using drone launch counts to assess Iran's drone capacity, drawing lessons from the 1991 Gulf War. It notes that U.S. battle damage assessments of Iraq's Republican Guard were found to be significantly flawed, with successful strike probability estimated at only 41 to 60 percent.
