stories.title: The Navy’s Latest Is Not a Plan, Not a Strategy, and Not Fighting Instructions
stories.summary: The article criticizes U.S. Chief of Naval Operations Admiral Daryl Caudle's new Fighting Instructions document as lacking a coherent strategic theme. It argues the Navy continues a pattern of issuing aspirational guidance without providing the concrete direction needed for force planning.

stories.title: How Iranians are evading internet blocks to contact family abroad
stories.summary: Iranian citizens are using various technological workarounds to bypass government-imposed restrictions on phone and internet connections in order to communicate with family members abroad.

stories.title: Will Trump help or hinder Zimbabwe's white farmers in their compensation battle?
stories.summary: White farmers in Zimbabwe seeking compensation for land seized under past reforms have hired a lobbying firm with close ties to U.S. President Donald Trump. The move raises questions about whether Trump will support or hinder their case.

stories.title: Ex-UFC Fighter and Kinahan ‘Friend’ Mounir Lazzez Linked to Iran Sanctions
stories.summary: An investigation by Bellingcat and The Sunday Times revealed that ex-UFC fighter Mounir Lazzez has links to Iran sanctions cases. Lazzez was previously photographed with wanted Kinahan cartel leaders Daniel and Christy Kinahan at a fighting championship event in Dubai.

stories.title: Russia created an elite hit squad to target its opponents abroad. One of its agents was compromised by using Google Translate.
stories.summary: Russia established a secret elite intelligence unit in late 2022 tasked with carrying out assassinations, abductions, and sabotage abroad. An investigation by The Insider revealed that one agent compromised the entire group by using Google Translate.

stories.title: Under drone fire, exiled Kurds wait to confront Iranian regime
stories.summary: A group of exiled Kurdish fighters based in Iraq say they are prepared to return to Iran, even as they face drone attacks launched by Tehran against their positions.

stories.title: A Ukrainian attack on a Russian missile plant killed at least seven civilians. Locals say they had nowhere to hide.
stories.summary: A Ukrainian strike on the Kremniy El microelectronics plant in the Russian border city of Bryansk on March 10 killed at least seven civilians and injured 42 others. Nearby buildings, including a technical college and residential structures, were also damaged. Residents reported having nowhere to shelter.

stories.title: Russia declares scholar Nina Khrushcheva, the great-granddaughter of Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev, a ‘foreign agent’
stories.summary: Russia's Justice Ministry has designated Nina Khrushcheva, a professor of international affairs at The New School in New York City and great-granddaughter of Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev, as a "foreign agent." The designation was published on Friday.

stories.title: U.S. temporarily lifts sanctions on Russian oil as Middle East war drives up energy prices
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department temporarily eased sanctions on Russian oil currently at sea. The exemptions, issued on Thursday, are set to remain in effect until April 11, as rising energy prices linked to the Middle East war prompted the move.

stories.title: His film ‘Mr. Nobody Against Putin’ is up for an Oscar — but its ethics are under scrutiny. Here’s what Pavel Talankin has to say.
stories.summary: The documentary "Mr. Nobody Against Putin," about wartime propaganda targeting schoolchildren in the Russian town of Karabash, has been nominated for Best Documentary Feature at the 2025 Oscars. The film previously won a Special Jury Prize at Sundance 2025 and a BAFTA, but co-director and narrator Pavel Talankin faces criticism over ethical concerns about how footage was obtained.

stories.title: Iranians react to new supreme leader's first address
stories.summary: Iranians are reacting to the first public address by new supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, which was delivered via a state TV presenter rather than in person, raising questions about who holds actual power.

stories.title: As hopes of regime change in Iran fade, Netanyahu faces political test
stories.summary: As prospects for regime change in Iran diminish, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu faces growing political pressure. Israeli leaders are characterizing the bombing campaign as having reshaped the Middle East in Israel's favor.

stories.title: Southeast Asia’s Nuclear Blind Spot: Latent Pathways and Explicit Pressures
stories.summary: Despite Southeast Asia's Nuclear Weapon-Free Zone and strong anti-nuclear norms, the region faces growing nuclear risks from the diffusion of nuclear-adjacent capabilities. Shifts in maritime strategy, civilian nuclear development, and broader East Asian nuclear dynamics are increasing the region's vulnerability.

stories.title: Military Senior Service Colleges Require Reform, But There Sure Are Some Bad Ideas Out There
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered a review of the military's senior service and war colleges and severed ties with 22 academic institutions. The article argues reform is needed but warns against misguided approaches that could undermine critical thinking in military education.

stories.title: 'There's no hiding place on a ship': The sailors stranded near Iran
stories.summary: Sailors stranded on ships in the Persian Gulf are witnessing frequent drone, cruise missile, and fighter jet activity as the US-Iran conflict continues to disrupt maritime operations in the region.

stories.title: Mission accomplished? The 2003 boast that haunts today's Iran conflict
stories.summary: Analysts are drawing comparisons between the current US-Iran conflict and the 2003 Iraq War, particularly the premature "mission accomplished" declaration, while noting significant differences between the two conflicts.

stories.title: Punishing the Crocus perpetrators: The closed-door trial over Russia’s deadliest terrorist attack in decades ends with 15 life sentences and lingering questions
stories.summary: A Moscow court on March 12, 2026, sentenced nearly all defendants to life in prison following a closed-door trial over the March 2024 Crocus City Hall attack outside Moscow. The attack killed at least 150 people when gunmen opened fire and set fire to the venue. Four gunmen and 15 alleged accomplices stood trial.

stories.title: 'Follow the smoke': BBC spends day with emergency teams as Israel strikes south Lebanon
stories.summary: The BBC visited Nabatieh in southern Lebanon, documenting the intensity and scale of Israeli airstrikes as the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah continues to escalate.

stories.title: Tracking the wave of ship attacks that has choked off Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Six ships were reportedly attacked in the Persian Gulf within 48 hours, bringing the total number of vessels struck during the US-Iran war to 18 and further choking off traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: A Russian schoolteacher smuggled footage abroad and made an award-winning documentary about wartime propaganda. Here’s how his hometown reacted.
stories.summary: Pavel Talankin, a 34-year-old school events coordinator from Karabash, secretly filmed patriotic school events and smuggled the footage abroad to co-direct the Oscar-nominated documentary "Mr. Nobody Against Putin." Russian media labeled the film "anti-patriotic" and called Talankin a traitor after its Western release.

stories.title: How Iran war laid bare the world's reliance on Gulf oil and gas
stories.summary: The US-Iran war has exposed global dependence on Gulf oil and gas, with countries worldwide experiencing the economic impact of the conflict and resulting energy price shocks.

stories.title: 'What if we're left with ruins?': Doubts creep in for Iranians who supported war
stories.summary: Iranian civilians, including teachers, engineers, and shopkeepers, who initially supported the war effort are expressing growing doubts and fears that Iran could descend into chaos.

stories.title: One house, two faiths, one fasting season
stories.summary: In Nigeria, couples like Olanrewaju and Kaosara are observing Ramadan and Lent simultaneously in the same household. The two religious fasting seasons have overlapped for the first time since 1993.

stories.title: Magazine Breadth — Not Just Depth — Is Key to Munitions Industrial Base Resilience
stories.summary: The U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran have depleted stores of precision-guided munitions and interceptors, creating risk for other potential theaters such as East Asia. The article argues that breadth of munition types across the industrial base—not just stockpile depth—is essential for resilience.

stories.title: Testing Denial: The Philippine Alliance in America’s First Island Chain Strategy
stories.summary: The article examines the U.S.-Philippines alliance in the context of America's first island chain denial strategy in the Indo-Pacific. It argues that alliance credibility depends on the Philippines' ability to sustain operations under fire, including repairing critical infrastructure like runways.

stories.title: A Blank Check for Israel and the War with Iran
stories.summary: The United States entered the war with Iran not because of a direct attack but after concluding that Israel's military action made American involvement unavoidable. Secretary of State Marco Rubio briefed congressional leaders days before strikes began, with debate centering on whether to strike alongside Israel or wait for Iranian retaliation.

stories.title: Russia’s return to the Venice Biennale has triggered backlash and a threat to pull E.U. funding. Meduza explains how the forum was designed for soft power from the start.
stories.summary: Russia plans to reopen its national pavilion at the 2026 Venice Biennale for the first time since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Kremlin cultural envoy Mikhail Shvydkov confirmed an exhibition will open in May. The announcement has drawn backlash, including threats to pull E.U. funding from the event.

stories.title: Kazakhstan is reportedly preparing for a mass deportation of anti-war Russians. Is anywhere safe for those fleeing Kremlin repressions?
stories.summary: Kazakhstan's intelligence agency has opened a major criminal case targeting Russians living in the country, with dozens of draft-age men called in for questioning. Human rights defenders warn the investigation may serve as cover for a large-scale deportation campaign coordinated with Moscow, further narrowing options for Russians who fled after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: How China Views the Cognitive Element of a War for Taiwan
stories.summary: The article revisits a 2022 analysis of China's plans for AI-enabled cognitive warfare in a potential Taiwan conflict. Four years later, it reassesses China's progress in developing thought-manipulation capabilities as AI technology has become more advanced.

stories.title: Tracing Tomahawks: US Missiles Bound for Iran Spotted Over Iraq
stories.summary: Bellingcat geolocated footage showing multiple US Tomahawk cruise missiles traveling through Iraqi airspace toward Iran. At least 20 individual missiles were identified over Iraqi Kurdistan, raising questions about whether they transited with Iraq's consent or in violation of its airspace.

stories.title: What we know about Ukraine’s missile attack on a microchip plant in southwestern Russia
stories.summary: A missile strike on the Russian city of Bryansk on Tuesday killed six people and injured at least 42 others, according to local authorities. The attack targeted a microchip plant in southwestern Russia.

stories.title: Lessons from Ukraine for Defending Gulf Airspace from Shaheds
stories.summary: In early March 2026, a drone strike at Port Shuaiba in Kuwait killed six American servicemembers—the first U.S. fatalities of the Iran conflict. The article draws lessons from Ukraine's counter-drone experience, highlighting detection challenges and the cost imbalance between cheap drones and expensive interceptors like Patriot missiles.

stories.title: Indonesia’s Blue-Water Ambition Requires Sustained Overseas Deployments
stories.summary: Indonesia is expanding its naval fleet with larger, more capable platforms including combat ships from Italy, frigates from Turkey, and Arrowhead 140 frigates from the United Kingdom. The article argues that achieving blue-water ambitions will require sustained overseas deployments beyond simply acquiring new vessels.

stories.title: Gaza and the Logic of High-Intensity Urban Warfare
stories.summary: The article argues that the Gaza War between Israel and Hamas should be analyzed as high-intensity urban warfare rather than measured against counterinsurgency standards from Iraq and Afghanistan. It contends that applying an inappropriate analytical framework has led to flawed assessments of the conflict.

stories.title: ‘World War III is already underway’: Zelensky advisor Mykhailo Podolyak on what the new Middle East war means for Ukraine
stories.summary: Senior Ukrainian presidential adviser Mykhailo Podolyak discussed the intersection of the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East with Meduza. Since the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran began in late February, Ukraine has warned the new conflict could reduce weapons availability for Kyiv. Meanwhile, Ukraine has sent drone-defense experts to help U.S. allies in the Gulf counter Iranian strikes.

stories.title: Arab States Scramble to Adapt to New Regional War
stories.summary: Since the U.S.-Israeli airstrikes against Iran began on February 28, Iran has retaliated with missile and drone strikes hitting military and civilian targets across Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE, Oman, and Jordan. The war has ended a recent warming in relations between Iran and several Gulf Arab states.

stories.title: Russia sentences Meduza journalist Dmitry Kuznets to 2.5 years in prison in absentia
stories.summary: A Moscow court sentenced Meduza military analyst Dmitry Kuznets to 2.5 years in prison in absentia. He was convicted on charges of participating in the activities of an organization designated as "undesirable" by Russian authorities.

stories.title: Middle East war delays Ukraine–Russia peace talks as Trump administration weighs lifting oil sanctions
stories.summary: The United States has delayed the next round of trilateral talks with Ukraine and Russia due to the escalating war in the Middle East, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. The announcement came on Tuesday.

stories.title: Fighting for Relevance Isn’t Everything
stories.summary: This edition of The Ukraine Compass curates Ukrainian media commentary and analysis for War on the Rocks members. It highlights how Ukrainians debate issues beyond the battlefield, including daily life, politics, and public discourse during wartime.

stories.title: A Worst-Case Scenario for the War with Iran
stories.summary: The article examines worst-case scenarios for the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, questioning whether the conflict could extend far beyond the White House's projected four-to-six-week timeline. It considers risks including regime collapse, regional chaos, and consequences for Gulf states, Israel, Iraq, and Lebanon.

stories.title: We Were Right About Havana Syndrome
stories.summary: A former senior U.S. intelligence official describes a debilitating health incident experienced in Moscow in 2017, later diagnosed as a traumatic brain injury at Walter Reed. The account supports claims that Havana Syndrome incidents represent genuine attacks on U.S. personnel.

stories.title: AI-Ready Biodata Is America’s Next Strategic Infrastructure
stories.summary: U.S. policymakers have prioritized AI leadership through significant investment but have largely overlooked the convergence of AI with biotechnology. Analysts warn this gap could undermine America's position in the broader global technology competition, as the fusion of AI and biotech is expected to shape economic and national power in coming decades.

stories.title: AI and the New Blueprint of Terrorism
stories.summary: Analysts warn that advances in AI, robotics, energy production, and sensor technology are enabling increasingly small groups to carry out targeted violence more effectively and from greater distances. This democratization of advanced violence is expected to affect state-on-state warfare, low-intensity conflict, and internal security enforcement.

stories.title: As War With Iran Rages, the Axis of Resistance is in Survival Mode
stories.summary: Despite the killing of senior leaders and sustained U.S. and Israeli military operations against allied groups, Iran's "axis of resistance" network continues to operate across Beirut, Baghdad, and the wider Middle East. U.S. forces have struck groups linked to Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces, while Israel has conducted operations against Hizballah in southern Lebanon and Beirut.

stories.title: Video Shows US Tomahawk Missile Strike Next to Girls’ School in Iran
stories.summary: Geolocated video footage shows a US Tomahawk missile striking an IRGC facility in Minab, Iran, on February 28. The footage, verified by Bellingcat, also reveals smoke rising near a girls' school adjacent to the targeted site.

stories.title: New Footage Shows Wanted Kinahan Cartel Kingpins Post-Sanctions
stories.summary: Bellingcat and The Sunday Times published photographs showing wanted Kinahan cartel leaders Daniel and Christy Kinahan in Dubai. The images represent the most recent confirmed sighting of the crime bosses since the US government placed multi-million dollar bounties on them.

stories.title: The Incendiary Bomb Never Seen in Israel Before
stories.summary: Bellingcat reported that the Israeli Air Force dropped 5,000 bombs on Iran following a joint US-Israeli attack launched the previous week. Bellingcat monitored weapons used in the initial days of the conflict, including a previously unseen incendiary bomb and strikes causing civilian harm.

stories.title: China spent years building ties in Latin America. Can Trump make room for the US?
stories.summary: President Trump is planning to meet with ideologically aligned Latin American leaders to counter China's growing influence in the region. China has spent years building economic and diplomatic ties across Latin America.

stories.title: Trump sets his sights on crisis-hit Cuba after Iran action
stories.summary: President Trump has turned attention to crisis-hit Cuba following U.S. military action against Iran. Trump claimed Cuban authorities are eager to negotiate a deal with Washington.

stories.title: Why Washington’s Kurdish Gambit Could Backfire in Iran
stories.summary: Analysts argue the Trump administration should abandon plans to arm Iranian Kurdish forces, warning the operation would not topple Iran's regime. Critics contend it would inflame Persian nationalism and provide Tehran a tool to fracture opposing coalitions, ultimately undermining American strategic interests in the region.

stories.title: Quenching the Nuclear Stockpile’s Thirst for Tritium
stories.summary: The article traces the history of tritium's role in the U.S. nuclear stockpile, from the Manhattan Project-era push to develop hydrogen weapons using deuterium and tritium fusion. It examines ongoing challenges in maintaining adequate tritium supplies for the nation's thermonuclear arsenal.

stories.title: War in Iran Shapes Adversaries’ Calculations
stories.summary: Since February 28, the United States and Israel have conducted joint military strikes against Iran, targeting senior officials including Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, missile facilities, naval assets, and regime security sites. The article assesses how adversaries including China, Russia, North Korea, and jihadist groups are recalculating in response to the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Inside Ethiopia's 'smart' police station
stories.summary: Ethiopia has unveiled its first unmanned "smart" police station, where citizens can report crimes using automated touch screens. The facility represents a step toward modernizing law enforcement in the country.

stories.title: Why a $1.5 Trillion Defense Budget Request Might Slow the Pentagon’s Reform Efforts
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced in January 2026 a proposed $1.5 trillion defense budget for fiscal year 2027, representing roughly a 50 percent increase over the previous year's request. Analysts suggest this massive spending increase could paradoxically hinder Pentagon reform efforts by reducing pressure for efficiency and prioritization.

stories.title: The Bay of Bengal Flank: India’s Three-Front Dilemma and Its Implications for Taiwan
stories.summary: Analysts argue India's strategic posture across multiple fronts—including the Himalayas, Pakistan, and the Bay of Bengal—is a significant variable in whether China might attack Taiwan. India's ability to create risk for Beijing is increasingly shaped by a three-front dilemma that extends beyond traditional land-border tensions.

stories.title: Fighting an Economic War Without Fused Intelligence
stories.summary: A policy series examines how the United States lacks adequate integration of classified intelligence into economic statecraft and national security strategy. The analysis argues that intelligence gaps in economic decision-making undermine America's ability to wage effective economic warfare.

stories.title: Bonus In Brief: Global Reaction to the War in Iran
stories.summary: On February 28, the United States and Israel launched major strikes against Iran, killing Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and other senior officials. Iran retaliated with strikes against U.S. military sites, Israel, and economic and civilian targets in Arab Gulf states. Five experts assess the global reaction to the escalating conflict.

stories.title: What Recent Military Operations Signal About Trump’s Grand Strategy
stories.summary: Analyst Joshua Rovner revisits his 2025 argument about contradictions in President Trump's grand strategy amid escalating Middle East conflict. The piece examines what recent U.S. military operations—from the Caribbean to Iran to Nigeria—signal about the administration's broader strategic approach.

stories.title: The Velocity Gap Between Pakistan and India
stories.summary: Pakistan's post-2025 defense reorganization, aligned with its 27th constitutional amendment, reflects a growing emphasis on decision-making speed over raw military capability. Analysts argue that in South Asian crises, the velocity of coordinated action—assigning responsibility, authorizing operations, and shaping narratives—matters more than material strength.

stories.title: The Burden That Should Not Be Theirs: How Congress Turned the Military into the Last Check on Illegal War
stories.summary: Congressional Democrats have called on the military to refuse potentially unlawful war orders, effectively positioning service members as a check on executive authority. Critics argue this shift, caused by Congress's failure to exercise its own war powers, corrodes civilian control of the military and sets a dangerous precedent.

stories.title: Increasing Tensions Between China and Japan Create Risks for the Region
stories.summary: Tensions between China and Japan have escalated since November after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi suggested Japan could respond militarily if China attacked Taiwan. Takaichi has pledged to increase defense spending, and a major February electoral victory strengthened her position. Four experts assess the regional risks of this friction.

stories.title: Why Satellites Fail — and How to Protect Them
stories.summary: Jean-François Morizur, CEO of French company Cailabs, discusses ground-to-satellite laser optical communications and the emerging satellite-protection industry. The interview examines real-world capabilities that could threaten satellite communications and technologies being developed to defend them.

stories.title: Foundry, Fleet, and Fight: Hedging the U.S. Navy
stories.summary: U.S. Navy Chief of Naval Operations Admiral Daryl Caudle has published new U.S. Navy Fighting Instructions in response to growing operational demands. The Navy has conducted combat operations from the Caribbean to Iran to Nigeria during the current administration, underscoring the need for force readiness and modernization.

stories.title: Missed Signals and Middle East Shockwaves
stories.summary: Ukrainian media commentary examines how the U.S.-Iran war has sent shockwaves through the Middle East, with implications for Ukraine's own conflict. The digest curates Ukrainian perspectives on signals that may have been missed in the lead-up to the escalation and its broader geopolitical effects.

stories.title: Flying oranges: Italian town celebrates carnival with historic street battle
stories.summary: The town of Ivrea in northern Italy launched its annual Battle of the Oranges, a historic carnival tradition in which participants hurl oranges at each other in a large-scale street fight.

stories.title: At the scene: Muslims killed 'over rejection of extremist ideology' in Nigeria
stories.summary: At least 78 bodies have been buried following an attack on Muslims in Nigeria, reportedly carried out over their rejection of extremist ideology. The actual death toll is feared to exceed 170 people.

stories.title: 'The water took everything': Mozambique hit by worst floods in decades
stories.summary: Severe flooding in Mozambique has affected nearly 700,000 people in what authorities describe as the worst floods in decades. Weeks of heavy rains have caused widespread destruction across the country.

stories.title: From the front lines to the future: Israeli society and the Jewish people in 2036
stories.summary: At the Jerusalem Post Miami Conference, IDF veterans and civil-society leaders discussed Israeli society's future through 2036, emphasizing military service, human dignity, and Diaspora responsibility.

stories.title: How TALMA turns English education into social mobility and a Zionist mission
stories.summary: At the Jerusalem Post Miami Conference, TALMA CEO Ido Mahatzri presented the organization's work using English-language education to promote social mobility in Israel's peripheral communities.

stories.title: 'Over 90% of Iranians hate the regime,' INSS’s Beni Sabti reveals from leaked Iran survey
stories.summary: Beni Sabti of Israel's Institute for National Security Studies cited a leaked Iranian survey alleging that over 90% of Iranians oppose their government. Sabti described it as a secret poll showing 92% disapproval of the regime.

stories.title: Alshareef: Israel, Jews, should help Iranians seek liberty to ‘repay debt to Cyrus’
stories.summary: At the Jerusalem Post Miami Summit, speaker Alshareef called on Israel and the Jewish people to support Iranians seeking freedom, framing it as repaying a historical debt to the Persian king Cyrus. Prime Minister Netanyahu voiced solidarity with Iranian protesters.

stories.title: Watch: The Jerusalem Post Miami Summit
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Post hosted its Miami Summit, featuring discussions on shifting geopolitics and Diaspora-Israel relations. The conference served as a platform for cross-continental dialogue.

stories.title: The gifts I have been given: Survival as a collective act in Sudan
stories.summary: The article describes collective survival efforts among communities in Sudan amid the ongoing conflict, highlighting mutual aid as a central theme.

stories.title: Hope and resistance: Slam poets capture the weight of war in DR Congo
stories.summary: Slam poets in the Democratic Republic of Congo are using their art to express themes of hope and resistance amid the ongoing conflict in the country.

stories.title: Beware the AI efficiency messiah
stories.summary: The article discusses concerns about over-reliance on artificial intelligence as a solution for organizational efficiency challenges.

stories.title: Israeli bombing exposes critical shortages in Iran’s healthcare system
stories.summary: The article examines how Israeli bombing campaigns have exposed critical shortages within Iran's healthcare system.

stories.title: Myanmar in-depth: Slow earthquake response underlines need to overhaul long-flawed international aid efforts
stories.summary: The article analyzes the slow international response to an earthquake in Myanmar, arguing it highlights long-standing flaws in the global humanitarian aid system that need reform.

stories.title: As Sudan army gains drive mass returns, mutual aid groups begin to rebuild
stories.summary: As Sudanese army territorial gains drive mass displacement returns, mutual aid groups in Sudan are beginning reconstruction and community rebuilding efforts.

stories.title: “Strength in solidarity”: How mutual aid is helping women survive Sudan’s war
stories.summary: The article highlights how mutual aid networks organized by women in Sudan are helping them survive the ongoing armed conflict.
